Through participation in this area, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority helps promote policy dialogue internationally and regionally on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draws insights from this to enhance the climate adaptation capacity of the Hong Kong financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is intensifying efforts to enhance market awareness and participation, provide necessary infrastructure and drivers, and support international initiatives to align with global standards. The Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Group (Steering Group) is jointly led by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission, responsible for coordinating the financial industry's response measures to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the government's climate strategy1. The work of the Steering Group is primarily based on its strategic plan, which outlines six key focus areas and five action plans to consolidate the Hong Kong financial ecosystem and build a greener and more sustainable future (Figure 1). Strengthen financial risk management related to climate, promote the circulation of climate-related information at all levels to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a global risk management center, enhance the relevant skills of industry professionals by facilitating risk management, capital allocation, and investor protection, strengthen public awareness and understanding to encourage product innovation and research measures, guide capital flows towards green and sustainable projects to seize opportunities brought by Mainland China, and develop Hong Kong into a green finance center for the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (Greater Bay Area). Efforts to promote Hong Kong's sustainable finance development through regional and international cooperation to date have made good progress by the Steering Group since its establishment. The current focus areas of the Steering Group's work include skills training and data collection within green and sustainable finance centers (see below), the green taxonomy (see Chapter 9, "Establishing a Green Taxonomy to Promote Green Financial Flows" on page 9), climate-related disclosures and sustainable reporting, and carbon market opportunities. Specifically, the Steering Group announced the preliminary feasibility assessment of carbon market opportunities in Hong Kong in March, and will support Hong Kong in developing as a carbon trading center in the region, including developing an international high-quality voluntary carbon market, and seizing the opportunities brought by Greater Bay Area cooperation. In December, the Steering Group announced a collaboration with CDP2 to enhance data availability in Hong Kong and strengthen sustainability reporting. As part of this collaboration, both parties will develop a climate and environmental risk questionnaire targeting unlisted companies and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), which will facilitate corporate sustainability reporting and assist financial institutions in collecting and analyzing company-level data for risk assessment and related business decisions. This is an important step in the Steering Group expanding the scope of data work coverage to include SMEs, an economic sector that was previously difficult to reach yet is important. The Steering Group established the green and sustainable finance centers in July 2021, responsible for coordinating the work of financial regulatory bodies, government departments, industry stakeholders, and academic institutions in training and policy formulation, and for establishing resources and databases. In the first half of 2022, the center launched three databases focusing on data, training information, and internship opportunities, assisting the financial industry and other sectors in accessing data and learning resources related to green and sustainable finance. The resource library provides data sources to aid industry talent training in assessing the physical risks in Hong Kong. The center assisted the government in launching the "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme" in December, providing subsidies to employees, students, and graduates participating in training and skills enhancement related to green and sustainable finance. Other measures to promote skills training include launching the "Sustainable Finance Internship Program" to create more internship opportunities for students, and developing a new module 3 on "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Banking Professional Qualification Framework" for bank employees. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has consistently actively supported the development of Green and Sustainable Finance in the region through the Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme. In November 2020, the International Financial Corporation and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched the "Green Commercial Banking Alliance," gathering financial institutions, banking industry organizations, research institutions, and innovative technology providers in the region to jointly develop a cooperative platform for green commercial banks. The alliance aims to enable commercial banks and other financial institutions to fully realize their potential, develop green finance as a mainstream core business, and promote the financial system's participation in global climate change-related activities. The operating method is to provide a one-stop mutual learning platform for financial institutions to obtain the necessary knowledge, tools, and information to formulate their own green finance roadmap, and to transform into credible green finance institutions that gather green finance leaders, connect green finance institutions in different emerging markets to promote communication, and explore cutting-edge issues to drive the global green finance agenda, unlocking endless green and climate-related investment opportunities. In June, five leading global financial institutions became foundational members of the alliance and closely cooperated with the International Financial Corporation and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to encourage clients to adopt green strategies, promote best practices in green products and services, and unlock new business opportunities, thereby helping to realize the green economic transition. In addition, three global partners and one knowledge partner committed in 2022 to provide climate expertise in areas such as innovation, standardization, and academic research. Details of the alliance and member structure are available on the relevant webpage (English version): The foundational members, the International Financial Corporation, and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority signed a Memorandum of Understanding. Furthermore, since March 2021, the alliance has jointly held 18 training activities and roundtable discussions, attracting over 6,000 participants from various global locations including Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. Furthermore, the alliance published its first cutting-edge research report titled "Climate Risk: Definition, Measurement, Current Practices, and Regulation" in June 2022 in collaboration with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Financial Research Centre (Research Centre). The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has consistently promoted green and sustainable debt issuance and built an ecosystem of local relevant professional services. The total amount of green and sustainable debt issued in Hong Kong in 2022 (including bonds and loans) reached US$80.5 billion, an increase of 42%. The issuance of $80.5 billion in green and sustainable debt, representing a 42% increase, demonstrates the government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and strive to develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city. In 2018, the government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme," and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority assisted in promoting the related green bond issuance. The government has issued nearly US$16 billion worth of green institutional and retail bonds to date, with the raised funds allocated to over 40 green government projects, including green buildings, waste management and resource recycling, energy efficiency, and energy saving. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the plan, the government annually publishes the "green bond report," detailing the allocation of funds raised from green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. To enable citizens to participate in the outcomes of sustainable development and sharing through investment in Hong Kong, the first tranche of green retail bonds, with a total value of HK$20 billion, was issued in May and received enthusiastic support from the public, becoming the largest green retail bond issued globally at that time. This issuance also expands the range of green and sustainable finance products in Hong Kong, consolidating Hong Kong's position as the leading green finance hub in the region and internationally. The government also continued its regular issuance of green institutional bonds during the 2022 to 2023 fiscal years, and issued green bonds worth US$5.75 billion in January 2023. This tri-currency issuance covers the US$, Euro, and RMB, with maturities ranging from 2 to 30 years, continuing to serve as an important benchmark for potential issuers in Hong Kong and in the region. This issuance was widely welcomed by the global investment community and successfully attracted new investors who had not previously participated in government green bond issuances, reflecting investor confidence in Hong Kong's long-term credit outlook and economic climate. The government has increased the issuance amount of RMB bonds to 10 billion RMB in response to investor demand. The shareholding of international investors and mainland investors participating in the issuance through the "Southbound Connect" via bonds has also increased, demonstrating Hong Kong's position as the primary offshore RMB business hub and further solidifying Hong Kong's leadership status as an international financial center. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also assisted the government in issuing tokenized green bonds in February 2023 to test the use of distributed ledger technology for bond issuance and settlement. This is the first batch of tokenized green bonds issued by the government globally. This primary issuance is settled on a private blockchain network on a T+1 basis, and the subsequent processes (including coupon payment, secondary market transaction settlement, and maturity redemption) are also digitized. This experience of the government's bond issuance can serve as a reference for market participants interested in similar bond issuances in the future. To provide the industry with credible and convenient market information, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to cooperate with the Climate Bond Initiative and the International Capital Markets Association to separately issue annual reports on the green debt markets in Hong Kong and in the region. The report by the International Capital Markets Association shows that in 2022, Hong Kong became the largest hub in the region for the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds, with the total amount of bonds arranged by Hong Kong reaching US$27.8 billion, accounting for over one-third of the total in the region. The largest arrangement for the Asia-Pacific international green and sustainable bonds was first issued in 2021 for US$27.8 billion, and the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government reissued RMB 5 billion offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong in November 2022, including RMB 2.6 billion in green and blue bonds. The Hainan Provincial People's Government also issued RMB 5 billion offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time this month, including blue and sustainable bonds. The aforementioned bond issuance activity repeatedly highlights Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable financing between Mainland China and various parts of the globe, as well as its long-standing position as the primary fundraising platform in the region. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to promote and implement the "Green and Sustainable Finance Support Scheme" launched in 2021, and utilizes this scheme to attract more relevant professional service providers (including financial institutions, green consulting firms, and external rating agencies) to establish and expand their operations in Hong Kong. This plan is widely welcomed by the industry. As of the end of 2022, the program covered external assessment service expenses for issuers of green and sustainable debt instruments, including pre-issuance, post-issuance, or both, to help issuers ensure and demonstrate strict adherence to market best practices and international standards. Starting from March, the program will be optimized, lowering the minimum loan amount threshold for applying for external review fee subsidies for loans from HK$200 million to HK$100 million, which will assist smaller enterprises in obtaining green financing. Following the successful concept validation of tokenized retail green bonds under Project Genesis in 2021, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre of the International Clearing Bank have collaborated again under Genesis 2.0 to explore the technical feasibility of digital carbon offsets (also known as Mitigation Outcome Incentives, abbreviated as MOI), thereby enhancing the transparency, objectivity, and environmental elements of the green bond market. This project was completed in October 2022, successfully developing two prototypes to track, deliver, and transfer digital MOIs using blockchain and other relevant technologies.

As one of the world's largest asset holders and managers, the Monetary Authority plays a significant role in promoting green and sustainable finance development to support the global climate change agenda. The Monetary Authority is also a pioneer of responsible investment, having led investments in green and sustainable assets since before 2015, requiring its external investment managers to adopt the "Principles for Responsible Ownership" issued by the Securities and Futures Commission, and to integrate environmental, social, and governance factors into the investment management of foreign exchange funds. The Monetary Authority prudently invests according to the principle of "preserve principal first, long-term appreciation," believing that emphasis on environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors can unlock long-term sustainable value and mitigate related risks for investments. Facing increasingly severe climate change challenges, the Monetary Authority continues to advance on the journey of responsible investment, including setting the "net-zero emissions by 2050" target in 2022 and optimizing risk management strategies to enhance the resilience of asset portfolios, thereby seeking more favorable risk-adjusted long-term returns for foreign exchange funds. The Monetary Authority is also actively involved in building a green and sustainable financial ecosystem, collaborating with investors and regulatory bodies with similar philosophies to promote responsible investment, and cooperating with international organizations to establish ESG investment standards. The transparency of climate-related information plays a significant role in managing climate risks. To fulfill its commitment to the Glasgow Declaration issued at the 2021 UN Climate Change Conference and the commitment to a green global financial system by the central bank and regulatory bodies, the Monetary Authority has made climate-related disclosures for foreign exchange funds in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) under the purview of the Financial Stability Board. a. FCLTGlobal — Focusing Capital on the Long Term b. PRI — Principles for responsible investment c. NGFS — Central bank and regulatory bodies green finance network d. TCFD — Task Force on climate-related financial-disclosures The Director of the Ministry of Finance chairs the advisory committee for foreign exchange funds, which establishes the framework and guiding principles for responsible investment and implements them in the investment management of foreign exchange funds through the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office. The primary guiding principle is for the Monetary Authority to prioritize ESG investments with risk-adjusted long-term returns comparable to other assets to implement the investment objectives of the foreign exchange funds. Details regarding the Monetary Authority's responsible investment framework can be found on the Monetary Authority website: The investment committee under the advisory committee for foreign exchange funds is chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority and is responsible for overseeing the ESG and climate-related risks associated with foreign exchange fund investment projects. The investment committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policy, and through regular meeting reports from the risk management and supervision department of the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office, monitors the progress of integrating ESG factors into investments and the ESG status of the foreign exchange funds. As shown in Figure 1, the ESG committee established under the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office is chaired by the Chief Risk Officer and is responsible for coordinating and supervising all ESG work of the foreign exchange funds. The agenda items and progress of work discussed by the ESG Committee at each meeting will be reported to the President of the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office of the foreign exchange funds. The dedicated team of the risk management and supervision department, responsible for the governance of responsible investment, and the various investment teams of the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office collaborate closely on integrating ESG factors, and assist the senior management of the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing the ESG and climate-related risks and opportunities of various investment items: Public market investments are monitored by the credit, compliance, and supervisory committees composed of senior management of the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office through regular reports from the risk management and supervision department regarding the ESG status of the asset portfolios. Furthermore, the risk management and supervision department also participates in the selection, appointment, and supervision process of external investment managers for stock portfolios from an ESG perspective (see the section "Actively exercising ownership rights" in the "Risk Management" section on page 27). The investment committee, chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority, will consider the ESG-related assessments made by the risk management and supervision department and the private market investment team for each investment recommendation in private market investments. Specific evidence further shows the significant impact of climate change and related risks. According to the latest report 3 of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (the Climate Change Convention), even if the nationally determined contributions announced by each region are fully implemented, the estimated global temperature increase by 2100 will still reach 2.1 to 2.4 degrees Celsius, making it difficult to achieve the goal of limiting the global average temperature increase under the Paris Agreement to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. If regions adopt more progressive policy measures to narrow the temperature gap, the transition risk⁴ and the repricing of assets by the market based on anticipated future trends, coupled with inherent physical risks, will all exacerbate the pressure on asset valuations. In view of the updated global warming trajectory and model assumptions, the Monetary Authority, leveraging the specialized knowledge of external consultants, further assesses the resilience of the "portfolio" of foreign exchange funds under the "rapid transformation" scenario (Figure 2), following the assessment conducted in 2021. The rapid transformation scenario includes higher transition risk factors in the short, medium, and long term, assuming that policy changes and technological development jointly drive a rapid decrease in carbon emissions, while various assets are suddenly divested to maintain the average temperature increase below 1.5 degrees Celsius before 2100. The disorderly scenarios suggested by the forward-looking climate impact assessment for NGFS are largely consistent. The portfolio can maintain resilience in the medium to long term because a larger proportion of the assets are sovereign bonds, which are less sensitive to the impact of the transition. Industry distribution is key. Low-carbon power and renewable energy assets can benefit from the relevant transition. Transition risk and the repricing of assets may have an impact on performance in the short term (especially equity assets). The overall portfolio will be increasingly affected by physical risks that gradually emerge over time. Energy and traditional utilities remain the most susceptible industries. The climate scenario and other modeling methods have their limitations. The analysis is based on the market benchmark industry distribution of strategic asset allocation and does not consider the effect of actively selecting specific securities within a particular industry. From more in-depth research, it is evident that investment items within a portfolio generally exhibit greater resilience against transition shocks or experience less severe impact compared to the market benchmark of strategic asset allocation of assets. This result once again affirms that the Monetary Authority's focus on responsible investment to counter climate change can enhance the resilience of asset portfolios. The trajectory of climate change remains unclear, and scenario analysis methods will continue to evolve with improvements in data quality and policy development. The Monetary Authority regularly reviews relevant scenarios and optimization assessments to more clearly confirm the resilience of foreign exchange funds to climate change. As a long-term investor, the Monetary Authority fully understands the risks and opportunities that climate change may bring. The Monetary Authority is committed to further expanding sustainable investment and seizing opportunities to address climate transition, mitigate climate risks, and enhance the long-term returns of asset portfolios. The Monetary Authority continued its good momentum in 2022, increasing the holdings of green, social, and sustainable bonds by another fifty percent. In terms of stock investment, the Monetary Authority invests in active stock portfolios with a governance theme, and adopts a decarbonization strategy focused on low-carbon emitting companies for passive stock portfolios. Furthermore, the Monetary Authority is discussing with the manager of the "long-term growth portfolio" of the foreign exchange funds the establishment of a dedicated private equity fund to promote green and sustainable development in the Asia region (Figure 3). Figure 3 continues to promote measures to increase ESG investment. The Monetary Authority has invested in the operation of an African-wide wind power generator, and in addition to producing clean energy, the operator also places great importance on social and biodiversity factors. Before the wind farm was established, local villagers used poisoned bait to prevent predatory animals from preying on their livestock, but this action inadvertently harmed certain endangered species of bald eagles. Livestock are important assets to local villagers, and to assist villagers in protecting their livestock, the operator has constructed livestock shelters within the wind farm to protect the livestock from predation by wild animals. Furthermore, the operator employs a sparrow surveillance team to issue warnings when bald eagles are attracted by animal carcasses incidentally left by predation, in order to shut down wind turbines and prevent the eagles from being struck by the blades. Reducing the situation where livestock are preyed upon brings a win-win outcome: on one hand, it secures the livelihoods of the villagers, and on the other hand, it reduces the incidence of bald eagles being killed by wind turbines, thereby protecting endangered species. Good ESG practices can bring more business opportunities to companies and open up revenue streams; the supply chain operations below are one example. The investment company is an integrated logistics warehousing operator in mainland China, specializing in cold chain medical, chemical products, and high-end consumer goods logistics services. The company faces continuously increasing ESG operational standards, primarily from multinational corporate clients requiring their service providers to achieve high carbon reduction targets in compliance with the Paris Agreement. In response to the relevant demands, the company has engaged an external consultant to assist in developing a "Three-Year ESG Plan" to reduce carbon emission intensity by 50% by 2030 or earlier. This comprehensive carbon reduction plan has already yielded significant results in 2021. The aforementioned ESG measures earned the company the "Low-Carbon Green Management Case" award from the China Logistics and Procurement Association. These achievements and accolades enable the company to gain considerable business opportunities from consumers and multinational clients in the chemical products sector who particularly emphasize ESG practices. The growth of ESG investment is closely related to the development of the green and sustainable financial ecosystem. The Monetary Authority actively cooperates with investors and partners who share similar philosophies, promoting responsible investment and enhancing industry skills. The Monetary Authority successfully hosted the 4th annual ESG workshop in 2022, facilitating exchanges on good ESG practices among nine participating private market institutions (including managing partners, limited partners, and corporations), and promoting sustainable investment opportunities in the Asia-Pacific and Greater Bay Area. In the public market, the Monetary Authority urges trading partners (mainly investment banks) to expand their ESG personnel and research capabilities, particularly in Hong Kong. Mr. Li Da-zhi, CEO of the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office, delivered the opening remarks at the Monetary Authority's ESG workshop in 2022 on an international level. The Monetary Authority is actively involved in formulating industry ESG investment standards and practices: as one of the earliest central banks to sign the Principles for responsible investment (PRI), the Monetary Authority participated in the joint action of signatories coordinated by the PRI to develop a uniform responsible investment due diligence questionnaire for private equity and venture capital investments, Nos. 5 and 6, to assist private market investments investors in assessing the ESG performance of managing partners and investment recommendations. The Monetary Authority participates in several working groups to support the research work of FCLTGlobal. This research aims to explore the main practices in the market for long-term investment portfolios and decarbonizing private assets, as well as the application of these practices for long-term investors. The Monetary Authority, as a member of NGFS and a supporter of TCFD, authored the NGFS's "Central Bank Climate-related Disclosure Guidance" to demonstrate the Monetary Authority's commitment to adopting good ESG practices. The Monetary Authority has established a working group under the NGFS's "central bank net-zero emissions" working group to participate in formulating the sustainable and responsible investment policies for central banks. The Monetary Authority continues to participate in various industry forums and lectures, sharing insights on responsible investment and climate change strategies. Ms. Liu Huijuan, Chief Risk Officer of the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office (China), spoke at the ESG Investment Opportunities Sharing Session, stating that building internal capabilities is crucial for continuing to advance the ESG journey for foreign exchange funds. In addition to encouraging employees to study relevant courses in sustainable development and obtain relevant qualifications, the Monetary Authority also draws relevant knowledge and practical experience from the process of receiving advice on the main industry practices for the climate transition of asset portfolios from external consultants since 2021. On the other hand, the Monetary Authority utilizes ESG data compiled by reputable external information providers to supplement its ongoing analysis of asset portfolios, in order to strengthen the ESG resilience of the foreign exchange funds.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to reducing its own institutional carbon footprint with the objective of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner, and to contribute to achieving Hong Kong's overall climate goals. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority strives to promote environmental sustainability on one hand, and fulfills its commitment to caring for employee physical and mental health, encouraging financial inclusion, and fulfilling social responsibility on the other. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to conducting daily operations in a responsible and sustainable manner. Therefore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority implements the concept of sustainable development under the three pillars of environmental, employee, and social responsibility (Figure 1). The corporate social responsibility and sustainable development committee is responsible for leading the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in formulating and implementing sustainable development strategies. The committee is chaired by the Governor of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, and its members include three deputy governors, as well as representatives from the Risk Management and Supervision Department and the Institutional Development and Operations Department. And submit periodic reports to the governing committee under the jurisdiction of the foreign exchange fund advisory committee. Under the leadership of the committee, multiple different teams and working groups are responsible for planning and executing the measures within their respective scopes. In 2022, the corporate social responsibility and sustainable development committee approved the organization's climate goals for operations and reviewed the transition roadmap to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. During the year, the committee will continue to review the progress of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's green measures, including recommendations to strengthen the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's sustainable development procurement policies, procedures, and methods. The governance framework for sustainable development; The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's journey of sustainable development is an acknowledgment of the Monetary Authority's commitment to the environmental, employee, and overall social, and the Hong Kong Social Services Association has presented the "15+ Together for Care" emblem to The Hong Kong Monetary Authority for the 16th consecutive year. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority pays close attention to its own carbon footprint and has established an internal "Green Office Guidelines" to control the environmental impact of operational procedures. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has integrated environmental factors into the office's interior design, operations, and maintenance and repair. In 2022, "Green Building Environmental Assessment" was granted a Gold certification by The Hong Kong Monetary Authority for certain office premises undergoing renovation. This is the second green building certification obtained after receiving Gold certification from LEED in 2021. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is implementing multiple energy-saving measures in the 1.0 version of the in-room building for the "Green Building Environmental Assessment." The total energy consumption in 2022 was 4,996.4 GWh (2.8 MWh per person), a decrease of 24.4% compared to 2015 (Figure 1). The total greenhouse gas emissions for Scope 1 and Scope 2 in 2022 were 8,299.64 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e) (1.7 tCO2e per person), a decrease of 38.2% compared to 2015 (Figure 2). Figure 1 Figure 2 Greenhouse gas emission density (Scope 1 and 2) The Hong Kong Monetary Authority encourages paperless operations within organizations. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority implements a printing management system, requiring employees to log into the printer to confirm each printing requirement, which helps reduce unnecessary printouts and toner usage. If printing is indeed required, double-sided paper and black and white printing are encouraged. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is also preparing to implement an internal electronic record-keeping system. The total paper consumption in 2022 was 20.5 metric tons (0.0114 metric tons per person), a decrease of 65.3% compared to 2015 (Figure A). (Figure A): The Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to implement the "4R" principles for waste management. In addition to traditional waste, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also reduces electronic waste by adopting technological solutions such as server virtualization and private cloud infrastructure. In 2022, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority first engaged an external company to audit waste and analyze the composition of waste generated by the office. This audit found that a large proportion of kitchen waste constitutes a significant part of the total waste, prompting The Hong Kong Monetary Authority to launch a kitchen waste recycling scheme (see page 41 "Enhanced Waste Management"). The total amount of non-hazardous waste generated in 2022 (including general waste and recyclable waste) was 242.0 metric tons (0.135 metric tons per person), a decrease of 4.8% compared to 2015 (Figure 3). The fluctuation in trends is mainly due to the implementation of work-from-home arrangements during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic and the resumption of office operations after the fifth wave of the epidemic. Figure 3: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority prioritizes source reduction of hazardous waste and is committed to reducing, reusing, and recycling. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority first engaged a company for audit waste in 2022 to more clearly understand the composition of waste in daily operations (plastics, paper, metal, glass, wood, electronic products, etc.) and to provide waste reduction recommendations. According to the audit results, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched a kitchen waste recycling scheme in November, installing kitchen waste collection bins in all pantry areas. Kitchen waste collected daily will be transported to an organic resource recycling center in Hong Kong and converted into renewable energy for power generation. The residue generated during the conversion process can also be made into compost for landscape beautification and agricultural production. Additionally, trash cans are provided in different locations in the office for convenience. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority shares recycling tips with employees and focuses further on improving source separation of recyclables, as well as precautions for handling recyclable items such as cardboard boxes, food containers, and beverage bottles. Furthermore, we continue to organize activities to raise employee environmental awareness, explain waste management policies, and encourage employees to make good use of the recycling facilities in the office. Kitchen waste collected daily is transported to the organic resource recycling center for the recycling of plastics. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has two data centers (one for operation and one for backup). Since these two components account for the majority of the institution's overall energy consumption, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has implemented green design and multiple energy-saving measures, including cabinet-type air conditioning systems, light-emitting diode lighting equipment, and 24-hour monitoring of power efficiency. Following the advisory research on the green performance of the aforementioned data centers completed in 2022, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is preparing to implement recommendations to enhance overall energy efficiency. Preparations are also beginning for obtaining green data center certification. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority understands the importance of establishing a culture of sustainable development, and therefore regularly launches various programs and activities to educate and encourage employees to develop habits favorable to sustainable development and adopt green and digital working methods. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority shares green living tips with employees, as well as annual energy and paper consumption statistics for the entire office, reminding them to help address environmental matters at the individual level. Furthermore, employees are also encouraged to submit suggestions regarding sustainable development matters. Under the leadership of the senior manager of the administration department, a special team gathered employees from different departments to brainstorm and propose ideas and specific measures to promote an environmental work environment. Members of the special team also bear the responsibility of ambassadorship when launching new green measures. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority encourages the wider social adoption of more environmentally friendly methods and has introduced multiple measures to improve the operational efficiency of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the financial industry, and the overall economy, while minimizing resource consumption. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Electronic Submission Reporting System" (STET) is a one-stop platform that allows banks to submit documents to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority electronically, covering various periodic reports required weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annually. Another "e-Delivery" is a secure electronic communication channel that allows The Hong Kong Monetary Authority to send notices and guidance, etc., to banks. Both systems help save a large amount of paper every year. In handling bank complaints and enforcement work, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has taken measures to support paperless submission of documents, allowing bank customers to lodge complaints through electronic channels and online forms. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is also developing a new generation management information systems to promote complaint handling and the transition from paper records to digital records. To reduce paper use, the Central Securities Clearing System (CMU)9 has adopted digital signatures in its daily communications with its participants, including issuing notices, account opening and account termination letters, and responding to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, CMU will continue to explore more green measures, including the adoption of automated electronic procedures for internal and external communication. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority encourages the public to adopt more electronic payment methods, replacing cash and physical cheques, by promoting the use of the fast payment systems "ZhuanShuKua" and stored-value payment tools. For more information regarding "ZhuanShuKua" and value-added payment instruments, please refer to the chapter "Hong Kong's Status as an International Financial Centre" in the The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's 2022 Annual Report. Distributing electronic remittances is simple and convenient, and can reduce the use of physical remittance envelopes and banknotes, helping to promote sustainable development in Hong Kong. Therefore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to actively promote on various social platforms and traditional platforms, encouraging residents to distribute electronic remittances or other electronic wallet services via online or mobile banking services using "ZhuanShuKua" during the Lunar New Year. Major banks and electronic wallet operators also host various activities to attract users to use electronic remittances, such as providing user interfaces filled with New Year atmosphere, enhancing functions for greater convenience, and launching prize draws or cash rewards. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority promotes electronic remittances on social platforms for citizens who choose to distribute physical banknotes during the Lunar New Year, and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to encourage them to use "Ying Xin Chao," which refers to using old yet new banknotes for the purpose of sealing remittances. Ying Xin Chao can reduce the need for printing new banknotes, thereby decreasing the impact on the environmental. The rewards from the issuing bank indicate that citizens have increasingly accepted Ying Xin Chao new banknotes in recent years. The coin collection scheme reflects the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's efforts in promoting coin recycling. Coins collected through this program will be returned to the market to meet public demand, improve the efficiency of coin circulation, and reduce the need for minting. The program has two collection vehicles and has served over one million people, collecting a total of over 800 million Coins with a total face value of approximately 1.3 billion Hong Kong dollars. In 2022, approximately 78% of users chose to use some or all of their holdings as value-added to stored-value payment tools accounts. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Hong Kong Social Services Association have maintained cooperation, deploying collection vehicles to collect Coins from non-governmental organizations, dedicated to supporting social services. The coin collection scheme on the collection vehicles' coin counting machine was launched in 2014, being the world's first systematic coin collection program adopting the mobile vehicle concept, and has received multiple Hong Kong and international awards over the years; its innovative and environmentally friendly methods for handling Coins have been highly acclaimed. The program has two collection vehicles, each equipped with two high-speed coin counting machines to collect the Coins exchanged by the public. The public may choose to exchange Coins for banknotes, use them to top up stored-value payment tools (such as a bidet card or e-wallet) accounts, or donate them to public welfare funds as charity. In addition to collecting Coins, collection vehicles are also sometimes assigned for various educational activities (e.g., student tours).

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency independently verifies the climate targets of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). Climate targets are established in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Handbook ("SBTi Corporate Handbook"). The purpose of this verification work is to verify whether the climate targets have been established in accordance with the SBTi Corporate Handbook. This verification work is conducted in accordance with the "International Verification Engagement Guidelines 3000" (Revised Edition) issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board, specifically the provision for "Verification engagements other than the audit or review of historical financial data." The verification procedure is designed to make opinions and summaries to obtain a reasonable degree of assurance. The verification process is determined according to the requirements of the SBTi corporate handbook. The HKMA is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance and summarizes: • The climate targets are established in reference to the SBTi corporate handbook. Shen Xiaoyin reviewed the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency's March 2023 verification statement regarding the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency's independent verification of the 2022 environmental data ("2022 data") for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The 2022 data include the total energy consumption for 2022, the emission density of Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gases, the paper consumption density, the density and recycling rate of non-hazardous waste generated, and the changes in this data compared to the 2015 level. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emission data are compiled according to the GHG Protocol accounting system jointly published by the World Resources Institute ("WRI") and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development ("WBCSD"). The scope of verification covers data from January 1, 2022, to December 31, 2022, and also includes relevant data from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2015, for comparison of annual performance. The scope of verification covers a total of 6 office and warehouse assets, with 4 offices located in 1) International Finance Centre Phase II office, 2) Harmony Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase I, and 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and 2 warehouses in 5) Lokesung Industrial Centre and 6) Chongli Centre, located in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan, respectively. The purpose of this verification is to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from 6 assets. This verification work is conducted in accordance with the "International Verification Engagement Guidelines 3000" (Revised Edition) issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board, specifically the provision for "Verification engagements other than the audit or review of historical financial data." The verification procedure is designed to make opinions and summaries to obtain a reasonable degree of assurance. The verification process is determined according to the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The validation process involved tracing the selected sample data back to its source to test the integrity and accuracy of the data, as well as reviewing the basic procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducting reliability testing. The validation process also includes verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, visiting representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 data, and auditing representative data and information. The relevant original data and supporting evidence were also thoroughly reviewed during the validation process. The HKMA is responsible for information collection and reporting. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The verification team of the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency did not participate in the 2022 data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reasonably assures and summarizes the 2022 data: • The 2022 data is substantially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin, Supervisor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023

Expanding and accelerating climate action has become the most urgent issue currently. Almost half of the key decade for the climate crisis has passed. We need to reduce global carbon emissions by over 40% in the next decade to have a chance of keeping the global warming level within 1.5 degrees Celsius. However, greenhouse gas emissions continue to reach new highs. The latest climate science research indicates that the window of opportunity to control global temperature rise within 1.5 degrees Celsius will soon disappear. Everyone has clearly felt the impact of the 1.1-degree Celsius rise in temperature—record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding, and storms, etc., extreme weather events are occurring frequently in various parts of the world, and they are becoming more severe with each occurrence. Hong Kong was no exception; in September last year, after experiencing a fierce super typhoon, it was immediately followed by a century-scale torrential rain. Although we possess good infrastructure and can respond to disasters quickly, the impact remains very severe—flooding in wide areas, transportation disruptions, and damage to roads in many places. All these clearly remind us that decisive and proactive climate action is urgently required. Asia faces particularly significant challenges on the path to low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development and sustainability. We require a credible transition strategy that can appropriately balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means an easy task. Due to the rapid economic development within the region and the rapid population increase, its carbon emissions account for over half of the global total emissions. Furthermore, the Asia-Pacific region has a high population density, and due to its geographical location, it is also susceptible to the impacts of sea-level rise and extreme weather events. Due to the uneven development progress of economies within the region, while the low-carbon transition will bring new opportunities to some economies, raising the necessary transition funds presents a significant challenge for others. Market estimates that the annual investment required for the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region over the next 30 years will exceed $3 trillion. As an international financial center, Hong Kong possesses the capability and responsibility to utilize financial power to support the low-carbon transition of the entire Asia region. As a regulator of the banking industry, a promoter of the Market, and a responsible investor, the Monetary Authority has consistently made significant efforts towards the sustainable development agenda. Everyone can learn about the various specific measures and work introduced by the Monetary Authority over the past year from each chapter of this report. Furthermore, to strengthen the internal governance structure of the Monetary Authority and to more effectively coordinate the sustainable development work across different functional areas, we established the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee last year. For detailed information regarding the Supervisory Committee, please refer to the new chapter on "Sustainable Governance." Hong Kong banks play an important role in supporting the transition to net-zero emissions in Asia. In addition to fulfilling the traditional functions of the banking industry regulatory body, we play a facilitator role in daily supervision by ensuring banks properly manage climate risks, and supporting the banking industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a green classification framework to assist banks and other financial institutions in identifying environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. We launched a prototype of the green classification framework for consultation in May, and are currently optimizing the framework based on the feedback collected during the consultation period. Furthermore, in response to the increasing demand from various sectors for higher quality and globally comparable sustainability disclosure information, the Monetary Authority is collaborating with other regulatory bodies to establish a clear roadmap for Hong Kong, adopting the disclosure standards released by the International Sustainability Standards Board in June, which constitute a comprehensive global sustainability reporting baseline. The Monetary Authority's role as a facilitator is not limited to establishing frameworks and regulations; we are also committed to resolving pain points at the industry interface. Currently, many banks are limited by data and find it difficult to conduct physical risk assessment. In view of this, the Monetary Authority will launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform in the short term, allowing banks to simply input property addresses to assess the impact of physical disasters on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios, thereby assisting banks in managing related climate risks. As a major international financial center and sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong has consistently played the role of a bridge, guiding international investment towards sustainable development projects in the region and supporting the low-carbon transition. In recent years, the total amount of international green and sustainable bonds issued in Hong Kong has accounted for over one-third of the Asia Market, clearly leading other regions. It is particularly noteworthy that the Shenzhen municipal government and the Hainan provincial government issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong for the third and second consecutive years in 2023, once again affirming Hong Kong's important role as a green gateway connecting the mainland with other regions globally. The activities of sustainable bonds in Hong Kong are flourishing, partly attributable to the exemplary role of the "Government green bonds programme." Since 2019, the Monetary Authority has assisted the government in issuing green bonds valued at approximately 25 billion US dollars, sold to institutional and retail investors. We seize every issuance opportunity, continuously innovating and expanding the characteristics of green bonds, including currency, maturity, and distribution channels, to lay the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world's largest government retail green bonds in 2022, we issued the first batch of tokenized government green bonds globally in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the issuance of the second tranche of tokenized green bonds. This batch of bonds is denominated in four major currencies and issued in a digital native format, making it the first multi-currency digital green bonds globally. At the same time, we are also proactively introducing various measures to enhance the vitality and competitiveness of the sustainable finance ecosystem in Hong Kong. This encompasses work in various areas including skills training, data improvement, green fintech, and transformative finance. Specifically in talent training, in 2023, we launched a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the professional qualifications framework of the banks, providing systematic courses for bank employees to enhance their understanding and professional knowledge of green and sustainable finance. Transformative finance is another key area of our work, providing funding for decarbonization activities in high-carbon emission and hard-to-abate industries, preventing these sectors from failing to transform due to a lack of financial support. To support the stable development of transformative finance, the Monetary Authority will expand the Hong Kong green classification frameworks to cover transformative activities. We will also expand the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Support Scheme" for eligible bond issuers and borrowers to include transition bonds and loans, to encourage businesses in the region in Hong Kong to raise transition financing. Furthermore, we will strengthen communication and liaison with relevant stakeholders, attracting private sector investment into sustainable development projects that were previously difficult to finance through public-private partnerships and hybrid financial models. The aforementioned work requires cross-sectoral cooperation and is coordinated by the Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Group, co-chaired by the Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional cooperation is also equally important. In addition to our long-term cooperation with international financial institutions on the "Green Commercial Banking Alliance," the Monetary Authority's Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office also joined the "Sustainable Investment Capability Building Alliance" and the "Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership" in 2023, becoming a founding member. Furthermore, the "Glasgow Net Zero Finance Alliance" has also announced plans to establish a branch in Hong Kong. This is through these cooperative relationships, we hope to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, and subsequently support the channeling of funds to sustainable development projects in the region and globally. To promote new business development and knowledge exchange, the Monetary Authority also assisted in organizing the inaugural "Hong Kong Green Week" earlier this year, attracting over 1,600 participants from nearly 30 regions, including top decision-makers from the global business and finance sectors, to jointly discuss solutions for expanding climate finance in the region and to establish new cooperative relationships. Chairman Mr. Yu Wei-man delivered a speech at the focal event "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum" during the "Hong Kong Green Week," stating that the Monetary Authority, as the manager of Hong Kong's official reserves and a major global asset holder in the region, should set an example by being a responsible investor. Since 2015, the Monetary Authority has been leading green and sustainable asset investment, and gradually expanding the scope of foreign exchange funds in ESG and green asset portfolios across public and private markets. In line with the objective for foreign exchange funds' "portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, the Monetary Authority added a new active global equity investment portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition last year, while also expanding the application of a customized low-carbon stock index to another public markets asset portfolio. Furthermore, the Monetary Authority prioritizes investment in green, social responsibility, and sustainable development bonds, which outperform the investment benchmark, demonstrating the principle of "doing good and getting rich." In the private markets sector, we continue to pursue green-related investment opportunities and have become anchor investors for two transformation investment funds focused on Asia. By the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon density (WACI) of the foreign exchange funds stock portfolio decreased by 6% and 46% compared to the levels in 2021 and 2017, respectively, and has remained below the overall Market level. The Monetary Authority, as a sustainability organization, will continue to strive for progress and formulate our sustainability goals and plans based on the three pillars of environmental, employee, and social responsibility. Specifically, the Monetary Authority, in the journey of the low-carbon transition, continuously strengthens our capacity to address climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing different internal measures. This measures cover emission reduction, energy efficiency improvement, and waste management, with the ultimate goal of achieving our commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner. We have formulated a plan to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the short term and have made good progress towards the medium-term goal of reducing Scope 2 emissions by 2030. To attract and retain excellent talent, and to fulfill the Monetary Authority's various important functions, in addition to green objectives, the Monetary Authority is also committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of its employees. Furthermore, we contribute to creating a caring society by collaborating with various stakeholders to promote financial inclusion, enhance the financial literacy of citizens, and raise public awareness of financial fraud prevention. The climate challenge is enormous and extremely urgent. Economic systems worldwide are moving towards a more sustainable future, a process that is expected to bring significant changes to financing activities and asset allocation. This transformation carries considerable risk, but will also bring unprecedented opportunities. As a major global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in action to address these challenges. At the same time, we are also in a favorable position to ride the momentum. The Monetary Authority will fully support the industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition. Continuing as a responsible investor and sustainable organization, acting on principles and collaborating with like-minded partners, to advance this currently very important global agenda. Chairman Yu Wei-wen

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are global concerns. The Monetary Authority's objective in sustainable development work is to exert leadership through its own policies and operations to ensure that the Hong Kong financial system and the Monetary Authority itself can withstand the risks of climate change and support the transition to a more sustainable economic development. By actively participating in international and regional organizations, the Monetary Authority will also be committed to participating in the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards, from regional to global concerns. As a banking industry regulator, the Monetary Authority will further strengthen the banking industry's climate response and climate risk management capabilities. Specifically, the priority tasks include: launching a new round of thematic reviews and a new round of consultation meetings regarding the bank's climate risk management practices, as part of reviewing the progress of the bank in implementing climate risk management regulatory provisions. Continue the work on incorporating climate factors into the supervisory review procedures of the Monetary Authority. Complete the second round of industry-wide climate risk stress testing, provide guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and share observations and lessons learned with the industry. To enhance sustainable development disclosures, including cooperation with local authorities to align relevant regulations with the International Financial Reporting Standards for sustainable development as global benchmarks, and to prepare for the third pillar 1 framework of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision for climate-related financial risks, addressing global concerns. and guidance on the best practices for sharing transformation plans with the industry. To promote the healthy development of banks in providing green and sustainable investment products, the Monetary Authority will continue to closely monitor local and international market and regulatory developments, and maintain contact with the industry to ensure banks adopt appropriate sales practices. Furthermore, the Monetary Authority also plays a facilitator role, striving to promote the development of the green financial ecosystem and support banks in providing financing for economic transformation. We are about to release the local green classification catalog and will continue to expand its scope to include more activities such as transition initiatives. At the same time, we will also continue to explore the application of technological solutions to assist banks in identifying, quantifying, and monitoring their climate risk exposures. One example is the soon-to-be-launched cloud platform, which promotes the bank's physical risk assessment. To enhance the professional capabilities of employees, we will also develop a professional-level module in "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" in 2024. Hong Kong possesses superior conditions as a sustainable finance hub for the region and internationally. To fulfill this role, the Monetary Authority is assisting the government in implementing the proposals in the 2023-2024 "Fiscal Budget Proposal," expanding the scope of the "Government Green Bond Programme" to include sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bond market. Simultaneously, by attracting more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Funding Scheme." We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions, and enterprises to raise green finance through Hong Kong and explore the potential synergy between green finance and technology. Furthermore, we will continue to assist in promoting the government-subsidized "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme" to expand the talent pool for green finance in Hong Kong. As the Co-Chair of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Group" (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies and departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and work promoting the development of Green and Sustainable Finance in Hong Kong. The Steering Group will focus on three areas of work in 2024, including sustainable disclosure, the application of technology, and transformative finance. As another key focus, through the "Green Commercial Banking Alliance," the Monetary Authority and international financial institutions will continue to jointly launch various thematic programs in the Asia region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted professional training to banks, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in supporting financial institutions to establish their distinctive green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also be committed to deepening cooperation with the "Glasgow Net-Zero Finance Alliance," the "Continuous Investment Capacity Building Alliance," and green development investment and financing partners. As a responsible investor, the Monetary Authority commits the foreign exchange fund's "portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions targets by 2050 or sooner. We will continue to strengthen the sustainability of foreign exchange fund investments through a comprehensive and responsible investment approach, ensuring the resilience of the asset portfolio on the path toward net zero. We deeply understand that achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a comprehensive economic transformation; therefore, we are optimizing our net zero strategy, focusing on assets that bring positive climate benefits to the real economy while considering the objectives of foreign exchange fund investments. As an organization supporting environmental protection, the Monetary Authority's carbon reduction strategy will continue to keep pace with developments in the market, regulation, technology, and other climate-related areas. To further strengthen the Monetary Authority's climate response capabilities and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of utilizing technology-based solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our office. Furthermore, we will continue to actively encourage employees to participate in our sustainable development work, including launching promotional activities to foster sustainable habits and optimizing office procedures and practical methods. Furthermore, the Monetary Authority will continue to maintain consistent, efficient, and sustainable procurement methods, including evaluating suppliers' ESG practices when selecting and renewing contracts. Based on obtaining green data center certification in 2023, the Monetary Authority pledges to adhere to the specified certification standards. Regarding the regular updates of data center facilities, in addition to keeping pace with the latest technology developments, we will also incorporate green design and operational methods. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and recycling, and actively modernize internal systems to improve efficiency and minimize potential risks. Finally, in terms of social focus, the Monetary Authority will seek out more community service opportunities for colleagues, cooperate with the industry to promote financial inclusion and raise financial literacy levels, and enhance public awareness of financial fraud prevention.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating these impacts. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and the wider Asia region through its multiple roles as a central bank institution, a banking industry regulator, a market facilitator, a responsible investor, and a sustainability institution. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has a sound sustainable development governance framework that leads the formulation of relevant strategies and policies for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Supervise the implementation of relevant measures, and ensure that the operations and working methods of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority incorporate sustainable development factors. To strive for good corporate governance, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has established a sound sustainable development governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency for related work. The governance framework ensures that the strategic planning and decision-making processes of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority are effectively integrated with sustainability factors, and that effective mechanisms are in place to monitor and evaluate the progress and outcomes of sustainability work. The sustainable development governance framework of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority includes: the Foreign Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and relevant specialized committees, responsible for supervising the work of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, including the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's work in sustainable development and submitting recommendations. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Governor of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, is responsible for leading the overall Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) strategies and policies of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority at the management level. In terms of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office is responsible for coordinating and supervising ESG-related work within the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office. And regarding other functional areas, the relevant groups and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainable development measures for the development of the bank and the market up to the operations of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority itself. At the cross-sectoral level, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) jointly initiated the establishment of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Institutional Steering groups responsible for coordinating the work of various financial regulatory bodies, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion of the scope of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's sustainable development work over the past few years, we hereby established the Steering Committee in October to serve as a new central platform, leading and more effectively coordinating all sustainable development work across the different functional areas of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. To provide guidance for the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans related to ESG matters in the four functional areas of banking, market development, foreign exchange fund investment, and internal operations. Supervising the implementation of ESG-related plans by the various functional departments of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Assess the performance and effectiveness of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in achieving its ESG goals. and supervise the external communication strategy. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Governor of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, with three deputy governors serving as permanent members. Additionally, we will invite the executive assistants responsible for matters related to green and sustainable development to attend the Steering Committee meeting to report on the main achievements and future plans of their work. The Steering Committee regularly convenes meetings, and support is provided by the relevant working groups under the purview of the bank division, institutional development and operations department, foreign affairs department, and the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainable development measures, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission jointly initiated the establishment of Steering groups 2 in May 2020. The Steering groups, as an inter-agency platform, provide strategic direction and coordinate cross-sectoral work on how the financial industry should address climate and environmental risks, in order to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details regarding the work of the Steering groups, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Financial Ecosystem."

Climate change is a significant risk facing the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has always been committed to consolidating the Hong Kong financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face various impacts related to sustainability and climate in their daily operations. To continue to play its important role in the financial system and guide more capital towards green and sustainability projects, Banks must proactively manage climate risk. As a banking regulatory body, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is particularly focused on building the capacity of Banks to address and manage climate risk, and is accelerating the work of Banks to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to formulating various policy measures to strengthen the capacity of the Banks system to address climate risk. In August, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority issued a net-zero transition plan announcement, outlining high-level principles to assist Banks in maintaining safety and stability during the economic transition to net-zero emissions. After issuing the notice, we conducted a survey of some Banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transformation planning measures. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices regarding transformation planning with the industry and will host seminars or workshops to facilitate industry exchange of experiences. Regarding disclosure requirements, in response to the latest international developments, including the International Financial Reporting Sustainability Disclosure Standards published in June, and the consultation framework on the third pillar disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks launched by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision in November, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is strengthening its work to improve the sustainability-related disclosure framework for Banks in Hong Kong. Specifically, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is collaborating with local authorities and stakeholders in Hong Kong to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that complies with the International Financial Reporting Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority strengthened supervision of banks' climate risk management and provided advice to banks to help them further enhance their climate response and climate risk management capabilities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the regulatory framework for Banks. Climate risk management is now listed as a standing agenda item for prudential supervisory meetings held by bank management. Banking supervisors also adopt the enhanced CAMEL rating system, which incorporates climate risk factors, to assess the risk status and risk management system of the banks. As part of implementing the two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the regulatory framework for Banks, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has revised the "green" assessment framework to focus on the transformation planning measures of the banks. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is also reviewing the supervisory review procedures for assessing and monitoring the capital adequacy levels of Banks and determining their second pillar capital requirements, to encourage Banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to address climate risk. Following the completion of the 12-month implementation period for the "climate risk management" section GS-1 of the "Regulatory Policy Manual" under the two-year plan in 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched a special review of climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. This thematic review covers four main areas, including the governance framework for climate-related risks, the oversight of climate strategies, the oversight of climate-related risk management, and organizational culture, awareness, and communication. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has made several improvements to its climate risk stress testing framework, including the introduction of new 5-year scenarios to assess the potential impact on Banks from the simultaneous occurrence of economic and climate change shocks. As part of the stress testing programme periodically conducted by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, following improvements, the second round of climate risk stress testing commenced in June to comprehensively assess banks' climate risk exposures and further enhance banks' ability to manage climate risk. This is a risk stress testing exercise, involving 44 Banks, which is more than a sixty percent increase compared to the initial trial plan in 2021. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also held a climate risk stress testing forum in November, with more than 300 bank employees participating. By promoting the sharing of experiences among Banks, this activity helps deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review the progress of banks' implementation of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Regulatory Policy Manual" Unit GS-1 "climate risk management."
