The Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the management of Banks held a meeting to discuss their work in climate risk management and the common challenges faced in the industry, and to review the information and other public disclosures provided by the Banks to assess their progress. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority provides targeted advice to Banks, encouraging and supporting them to continue strengthening their climate risk management capabilities in line with the Monetary Authority's regulatory expectations. As global attention on Climate change increases and efforts to address related issues are made, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has noted the growing demand for green and sustainability investment products, and some Banks are also providing relevant products to meet client needs. In view of this, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has completed a special review of the banks' sales of green and sustainability investment products and issued a notice in November, outlining the standards the Hong Kong Monetary Authority expects banks to meet and sharing observations of good practices. This notice covers multiple areas including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and control, staff training, and bookkeeping records, aiming to reduce potential greenwashing risks and strengthen investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of related investment activities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to promoting the application of technology in the green and sustainability banking industry. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analysis, strengthening the ability of Banks to manage climate risk. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is about to launch a cloud platform trial version to allow Banks to assess the impact of physical risks under different climate scenarios on residential and commercial buildings. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to cooperate with other central banks and regulatory bodies to explore how technology solutions can assist in the assessment of physical risks. On the other hand, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) practices through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence to reduce the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched an online shared data submission platform, fully automating the data collection process for financial crime risk data, thereby strengthening the operational procedures for Banks to submit AML-related data in a sustainable manner. In September, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority organized the "Green Finance Technology Competition," aiming to seek solutions for market use to help the Banks address the challenges of the following aspects: (i) net-zero transformation or transformation planning. (ii) climate risk management; (iii) Green and sustainability finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted over 85 submission proposals from approximately 70 companies. In December, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority organized the "Green and Sustainability Banking Seminars," providing a platform for the banking industry and the technology sector to explore the role of low-carbon technology and green financial technology in the net-zero transformation in Hong Kong and Mainland China, and simultaneously announced the results of the "Green Finance Technology Competition." This event attracted approximately 400 participants from Banks, technology companies, regulatory bodies, and academia. To enhance transparency in the financial markets and bring green and sustainability finance decisions into closer alignment, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, with the assistance of consulting companies, is developing a local green classification framework. In May, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority published a discussion paper on the "Hong Kong Green Classification Framework Prototype," soliciting stakeholders' opinions on the establishment and implementation of a green classification scheme. Based on the consultation results, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is fine-tuning the framework prototype and identifying other aspects for the next phase of framework development. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority participates in the work of special organizations for financial action. The organization has confirmed the upstream criminal acts of money laundering for environmental crimes, and due to the interconnectedness between AML and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG), this scope is receiving increased attention from regulatory bodies. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is well aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system; therefore, broader climate factors and scenarios should be incorporated into financial risk analysis and research to strengthen current supervisory work. In the process of continuously monitoring financial stability risks, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will consider climate change and include an analysis of climate-related risks in all financial stability reports. Through active participation in the working group for scenario design and analysis under the "central banks and regulatory bodies green finance network" (NGFS), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority assists in further enriching climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulatory bodies to gain a clearer understanding of the impact of climate change on the macroeconomic and financial sectors. As a member of the working group for the transformation planning under the Financial Stability Board, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority participates in analyzing the interplay between the transformation planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to form a forward-looking and dynamic perspective for reviewing climate-related financial risks. In terms of research work, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority conducts multiple applied research projects exploring the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial sector and the economic. The research topics include the assumption of climate risk by the banking industry and investment funds2, the flow of ESG funds3, the impact of climate change on property prices4, and the ripple effect of corporate ESG in the global supply chain5. The above research findings enhance the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's understanding of the impact of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability, which aids in formulating relevant policies. Locally, this research helps strengthen the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's continuous monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risk on financial stability. Externally, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority also shares research findings with a broad range of stakeholders through various channels, including international activities related to climate and the "Hong Kong Monetary Authority Research Memoranda." The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Liquidity Funding Arrangement Framework" is a collateralized reserve funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework, as recommended by the NGFS. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and promoting sustainability finance as the mainstream. Through participation in this area, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority helps promote policy dialogue internationally and regionally on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draws insights from this to enhance the climate response capacity of the Hong Kong financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as the leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has worked closely with local and international partners to co-build a richer ecosystem and promote the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Group shall be jointly led by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission, responsible for coordinating the financial industry's response measures to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the government's climate strategy. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced the main measures to support Hong Kong in seizing the opportunities of sustainable finance, with the main areas of work including sustainable disclosure, strengthening the ecosystem, financial transition, and green finance technology. Specifically, the sustainable disclosure working group has been established to formulate the roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of IFRS sustainable disclosure standards. This roadmap will include four key areas, including sustainable reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. Another financial transition working group was established to explore methods for supporting financial institutions and enterprises in planning and reporting on their transition. The Steering Group also strengthens the construction of a sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sectoral skills training and data enhancement. Specifically regarding data, we continue to promote the adoption of the non-public company climate and environmental risk questionnaire 2, launched in 2022 in cooperation with CDP, by the Steering Group. The Steering Group will continue to closely follow the latest developments in the green and sustainable finance sector and enhance Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub in the region and globally. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key initiatives to seize the investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To provide skills training beneficial to the industry, the green and sustainable finance center under the jurisdiction of the Steering Group will implement the government's "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme," providing subsidies to employees, students, and graduates who receive training related to green and sustainable finance and obtain relevant qualifications. In December 2023, there were a total of 46 international and local training or qualifications registered as eligible training or qualifications under this program, and over 560 grant applications were approved. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has launched a foundational level of "green and sustainable finance" under the "banking professional qualifications framework." This module aims to promote talent development in the banking industry and enhance the overall professional capabilities of employees. In 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to collaborate with the banking industry to develop the professional level of this module to meet the industry's rapidly growing demand for professionals in green and sustainable finance. To help financial institutions and enterprises, especially SMEs, better understand key climate and sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management, sustainable reporting, greenhouse gas emission calculations, and transition planning, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, relevant government decision-making bureaus and departments, and global partners such as the CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ)3, and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financial (PCAF)4 will jointly organize a series of seminars and workshops during the year to attract participants from the financial services and corporate sectors globally. Regarding students, following the launch of the "sustainable finance internship program" in 2022, the training courses were held in January and February 2023, allowing interns and undergraduate degree graduates to deepen their understanding of sustainable finance. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority recognizes the potential of DeepMind Technology in filling data gaps related to climate and improving data quality, and is therefore committed to making the relevant data more accessible for viewing and use, and to enhancing data quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website optimization measures to provide a one-stop source of green and sustainable finance information for financial institutions, enterprises, and the public. Key optimization items include a sustainable disclosure electronic platform, greenhouse gas emission calculations and estimation tools, and more centralized, easily browsable, and searchable data and resources. During the "Hong Kong Green Week," the Steering Group also co-organized the "Leveraging Technology to Catalyze Sustainable Finance" activity with the Digital Hong Kong and Investment Promotion Agency to showcase leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's advantages in green technology. "Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Theme" was held from February 26 to March 1, 2024, attracting over 1,600 participants from nearly 30 regions, including representatives from financial institutions, enterprises, central banks, international organizations, government agencies, academia, and consulting firms, all with themes focused on sustainable development. The focal activity of the "Hong Kong Green Week" is the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum," co-organized by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and international financial companies. The forum gathered over 400 guests, including top decision-makers in the globally business and finance sectors, to discuss solutions for climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. The topic of the two-day activity exploration is quite broad, including energy transition, decarbonization of heavy industry, circular economy, the future development of sustainable finance, and new climate technologies in emerging and developing markets of the Asia-Pacific region. The forum has received responses from public and private organizations, co-hosting over 10 round tables, seminars, and other exchange activities. The topics cover climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition financing, green finance classification, and green development financing in the Belt and Road Initiative regions. In addition, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the International Monetary Fund co-hosted the "Asia Climate Finance Round Tables" on February 29, 2024, to discuss key measures for expanding the scale of climate finance, as well as the role of central banks and regulatory bodies in climate risk management. The above activities are part of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's overall work to promote and enrich the green and sustainable finance ecosystem in Hong Kong, serving as a useful platform to help participants drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address the challenges of climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has always actively supported the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, international financial companies and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched the "Green Commercial Banking Alliance" to jointly develop a platform for cooperation among financial institutions, the banking industry, research institutions, and innovative technology providers in the region for the development of green commercial banks. Since March 2021, the alliance has held a total of 22 training activities and round tables, attracting over 7,300 participants from around the globe, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. The alliance published a frontier research report titled "Developing an Aggressive Green Banking Climate Strategy: A Case Study" in October in collaboration with Crédit Agricole CIB on the topics of the banking industry. The alliance and Crédit Agricole CIB jointly published the frontier research report "Developing an Aggressive Green Banking Climate Strategy: A Case Study" on the topics of the banking industry in October. During the year, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office joined the newly established "Sustainable Investment Capability Building Alliance" (CASI) and the "Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership" (GIFP) initiated by the international "Belt and Road Initiative" green development alliance. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will aid in capacity training and knowledge sharing, and guide more funding towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and broader regions. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of a Hong Kong branch to support the net-zero emission work of financial institutions in Hong Kong and mainland China. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority assists GFANZ in a consultative role. To demonstrate the government's response to climate change, and its commitment to promoting green finance and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city, the government launched the "Government Green Bond Program" in 2018. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority assists in the issuance of green bonds under the program. The government has issued approximately $25 billion equivalent in green institutional and retail bonds to date, with the proceeds allocated to over 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recycling, energy efficiency, and energy saving. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the program, the government annually publishes the "green bonds report," detailing the allocation of funds raised from green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. The government continued its regular issuance of green institutional bonds in the 2023 to 2024 fiscal year, and issued approximately $6 billion equivalent in green bonds in June. This is a multi-currency bond issuance covering different maturities in the US dollar, euro, and RMB, attracting investors of various categories, with enthusiastic subscription, recording subscription amounts equivalent to nearly 30 billion US dollars. The issuance amount of RMB bonds increased from 10 billion RMB issued in January to 15 billion RMB, and a 10-year RMB bond was introduced for the first time, which will help extend the government's RMB yield curve and further enrich the selection of offshore RMB products. Global investors have reacted enthusiastically to the government's issuance of green bonds, reflecting investors' affirmation of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the government issued the second tranche of green retail bonds worth HK$20 billion, further promoting market development and advancing inclusive finance. This issuance provides citizens with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, allowing them to participate in and benefit from the development of green finance in Hong Kong.

As a major global asset holder and manager, the Monetary Authority plays a key role in promoting green and sustainable finance development to support the global climate agenda. The Monetary Authority has always been a pioneer of responsible investment. Since 2015, the Monetary Authority has been leading green and sustainable asset investment, requiring external investment managers to actively exercise ownership rights and to integrate environmental, social, and governance factors into the investment management of foreign exchange funds. The Monetary Authority invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "preserve principal first, long-term appreciation," believing that thorough consideration of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors helps to reduce related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of the investment. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and set a "2050 net-zero emissions" target for its "investment portfolio" of 2, the Monetary Authority is committed to continuously advancing its responsible investment journey, emphasizing sustainability, particularly the urgent issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of foreign exchange funds and pursue more desirable risk-adjusted long-term returns. As responsible investors, the Monetary Authority participates in building a robust green and sustainable financial ecosystem, collaborating with investors, regulatory bodies, and international organizations with similar philosophies to establish industry operational standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment by the financial industry and central banks. Through supervision and cooperative measures, the Monetary Authority is committed to promoting a future where finance and sustainable development run in parallel. Figure 1: Comprehensive and reliable ESG information for foreign exchange funds' responsible investment journey is crucial for integrating sustainability and planning credible climate transition to achieve net-zero goals. To fulfill its commitment to support the central bank and regulatory bodies' Green Finance Network (NGFS) "Glasgow Declaration" Clause 3 and the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Sectoral Steering Group Strategy Plan, the Monetary Authority is implementing, in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), this chapter on responsible investment for foreign exchange funds. The Foreign Exchange Funds Advisory Committee, chaired by the Director of the Ministry of Finance, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented in the investment management of the foreign exchange funds by the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. The primary guiding principles establish the tone for the Monetary Authority to practice responsible investment while also considering the investment objectives of the foreign exchange funds. The Investment Committee under the purview of the Foreign Exchange Funds Advisory Committee is chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority and is responsible for supervising the ESG and climate-related risks associated with foreign exchange funds investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policy, and monitors the implementation status through the regular meeting reports of the sustainable investment subcommittee of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office is chaired by the Chief Strategist and is responsible for coordinating and supervising all ESG work of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. The motions and progress of work discussed by the ESG Committee at the quarterly meeting will be reported to the President of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. Furthermore, the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee, chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority, the President of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office, and the Chief Strategist, convenes semi-annually to provide guidance on the ESG policies and measures of different functions within the Monetary Authority, including the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office, to implement the Monetary Authority's overall ESG objectives. Figure 2 shows the responsible investment governance framework of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office as shown in Figure 1. The Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office commenced the responsible investment journey in 2016, with the initial focus being on managing ESG risks that may affect the financial performance of the foreign exchange funds. As sustainable development rapidly evolves and becomes a priority strategic focus for major institutions worldwide, the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office has re-examined its responsible investment approach. July 2023 marked another milestone, with the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office establishing a new business strategy division led by the Chief Strategist, responsible for coordinating and leading the strategic development of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office, and incorporating the responsible investment task force, formerly under the Risk Management and Supervision Department, which is now called the sustainable investment subcommittee. This strategic adjustment reflects the Monetary Authority's shift in investment focus from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing investment matters related to sustainable development. The sustainable investment subcommittee and the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office collaborate closely in integrating ESG factors, assisting the senior personnel of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office in managing the ESG risks and opportunities, especially climate-related ones, for various investment projects: Public market investments—the situation where credit, regulatory, and supervisory committees composed of senior personnel from the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office review ESG factors after incorporating the opinions of the sustainable investment subcommittee into credit risk models, and the ESG status of fixed-income portfolios is monitored through regular reports from the Risk Management and Supervision Department. Furthermore, the sustainable investment subcommittee also participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring process of external investment managers for stock portfolios from an ESG perspective (see the section "Promoting the active exercise of ownership" in the "Risk Management" section on page 40). Private Market Investment— —The Investment Committee, chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority, will consider ESG-related assessments made by the Risk Management team on each investment recommendation for private market investments. The Monetary Authority understands that the physical and transition risks and related opportunities brought by climate change will affect the long-term performance and value of foreign exchange funds investment projects. The United Nations Environment Programme's "2023 Emissions Gap Report" projects that unless global greenhouse gas emission reductions are further implemented worldwide, the global average temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The urgent need for more progressive policies, technological development, or behavioral changes to control rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks such as asset devaluation or asset stranding. At the same time, extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and increasingly severe, also posing additional physical risks to investment projects. The Monetary Authority believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the investment objectives of foreign exchange funds, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG factors. The Monetary Authority established the target for the "investment portfolio" of the foreign exchange funds to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier in 2022, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The Monetary Authority will continue to strengthen its work across the three pillars and clearly focus on decarbonization and transformation. The following sections will detail the relevant methods. Figure 3 illustrates the Monetary Authority's dual approach to responsible investment in the process of moving towards net-zero goals, favoring proactive communication while avoiding the exclusion or divestment from its investable assets. First, maintaining a diversified and stable asset portfolio plays a key role in achieving the primary investment objective of foreign exchange funds. Directly excluding certain categories or industries will narrow the investment universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risk. Through compatible approaches, the Monetary Authority can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transformation and possessing excellent technology and good corporate governance to respond to changing global climate trends, including companies belonging to high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transformation of core "brown" industries. Only exclude relevant investment projects or divestment to help solve carbon emission problems. Conversely, the Monetary Authority supports these industries in implementing transformation to sustainable and low-carbon operating methods by investing strategic capital and actively exercising ownership rights, thereby bringing about beneficial changes for itself and for the global economy. In response to market development, the Monetary Authority is perfecting its net-zero investment strategy, employing comprehensive methods to strive for transformation outcomes that align with foreign exchange funds and global net-zero goals, while adhering to its guiding principles of responsible investment. The Monetary Authority continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities by integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, in order to promote climate transformation and enhance the long-term resilience of the foreign exchange funds asset portfolio (Figure 4). The Monetary Authority's responsible investment maintained a good momentum in 2023. In the public markets, the Monetary Authority is launching a new active global equity investment portfolio with a theme of sustainability and climate transformation, managed by external investment managers, and will expand the application of customized low-carbon stock indices to another asset portfolio managed by external investment managers. Furthermore, the Monetary Authority prioritizes the performance of green, social responsibility, and sustainable development bonds as investments that outperform investment benchmarks, demonstrating the philosophy of "doing good and getting rich." In the private market sector, the Monetary Authority is actively building robust long-term growth portfolios, seizing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic development trends such as climate and energy transformation. For example, the Monetary Authority invested in two Asia-focused transformation investment funds during the year, demonstrating the Monetary Authority's responsibility for addressing the needs of Asia's climate transformation. Figure 4 Measures to Continue Promoting ESG Investment The Monetary Authority has invested in a company that specializes in the production of eco-friendly thermoplastic plastic materials from unsorted household waste (including organic matter such as kitchen waste) and non-recyclable materials. Unlike traditional chemical recycling systems that rely on high-energy, high-temperature environments for plastic production, the company has pioneered a low-temperature production methods powered entirely by solar arrays. This plastic material, produced entirely from waste, can serve as an alternative to oil-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and durable consumer goods, offering a sustainable and versatile option. Through the MCPP programme, the Monetary Authority has committed to providing loans for sustainable development projects in 80 of 19 categories, including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate, and manufacturing, in 38 developing countries. The international financial institution collected data regarding the MCPP loan. According to the report of the international financial institution, the Monetary Authority's lending commitments provide support to emerging markets and developing countries in various areas such as economic transformation and human resource development. Specifically, the projects funded by the Monetary Authority are projected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 5.6 million tons of carbon dioxide equivalent annually, equivalent to the greenhouse gas emissions from a standard gasoline car traveling 14 billion miles. The Monetary Authority actively cooperates with investors and partners who share similar philosophies to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capabilities.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) is committed to becoming a sustainable institution, implementing multiple measures to reduce its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or sooner. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) also emphasizes employee physical and mental health and social responsibility, and strives to promote financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. As a responsible institution, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) sets sustainable development goals under the three pillars of environment, employees, and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), established in October, is chaired by the Governor of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) and is the principal decision-making body for various institutional sustainability measures. The Steering Committee was the predecessor of the institutional social responsibility and sustainable development committee, responsible for leading the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) in formulating the vision, strategy, and policies for institutional sustainable development and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Assistant Governor (Institutional Expansion and Operations) supervises the implementation of sustainability activities and regularly submits progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Special Project Team and Volunteer Service Team provide support for the institutional sustainable development work. The former serves as a platform for brainstorming how to create a green work environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of participation in volunteer activities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) has formulated a roadmap to guide its transformation direction. The focus is on implementing carbon reduction strategies in daily operations, including operating green buildings and data centers, practicing green commuting, adopting energy-saving measures, utilizing digital tools and more environmentally friendly operating models, waste reduction, and establishing a culture of sustainable development. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) also plans to utilize carbon embedding tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and for emissions that are difficult to reduce, it will adopt carbon offsetting measures. In addition to the environmental commitments related to its daily operations mentioned above, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) continues to introduce more environmentally friendly operational plans for the broader society, covering channels applicable to banks for submitting electronic documents and communications, as well as electronic payment and coin collection schemes for public use. To strengthen and maintain its operational capacity, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) has hired a professional working team, established a talent pool, and emphasizes the physical and mental well-being of employees. In terms of social responsibility, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) encourages employees to participate in volunteer and charitable activities. In procurement, consider selecting social enterprises. To promote financial services consumer education and cooperate with the banking industry to ensure that all segments of society can fairly access basic banking services. The remainder of this chapter details the specifics of the aforementioned strategies. Under the overall institutional risk management framework of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank), the risk committee, chaired by the Governor of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank), considers the potential risks and threats that The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) faces in its daily operations, including potential risks and threats caused by climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as more extreme weather causing flooding or other damage, may affect The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank)'s offices and impede employees' travel. To manage entity risk, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) regularly updates its operational plans to respond to extreme weather conditions. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility drills to ensure employees are always prepared to implement continuity of operations measures. The office design also incorporates multiple measures to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank)'s energy consumption, air travel, and waste management. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) continuously monitors the transition risks it faces by tracking its own greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank)'s climate goal is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across all scopes, including Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel), in the institutional operations by 2050 or sooner. As a recent emission reduction target, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all of its existing vehicles to electric vehicles. Using 2015 as the base year, through various carbon reduction and offsetting strategies, to reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier. Despite challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) will take a multi-pronged approach within feasible scope to minimize greenhouse gas emissions from Scope 3 (such as paper usage, waste generation, and air travel). The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets are formulated by reference to the "Science-Based Targets Initiative" methodology, a methodology that has also been verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) has commissioned the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency to verify the emissions, energy consumption, paper usage, and waste generation data disclosed in this report. The scope and criteria for verification are stated in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank), in addition to publishing the 2022 Annual Report, also independently published the 2022 Sustainability Report for the first time. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's efforts to strengthen ESG reporting have been recognized, receiving an ESG award in the "Public Sector Institutional" category at the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Award 2023." The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) is the first financial regulatory institutional to receive this award. The review panel praised The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) for achieving good ESG standards; the sustainability report is clear and easy to read, and the appointment of an independent institutional to verify its goal-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report reflects its commitment to high transparency and accountability in reporting. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) also received the highest rating in the "Non-profit and Charitable Institutional" category gold award in the Hong Kong Professional Association's "2023 Best Annual Report Award" selection. The review panel commended the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank)'s annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial data and for effectively utilizing infographics, demonstrating the Monetary Authority's commitment to enhancing financial knowledge and promoting financial inclusion. To commend The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank)'s commitment to caring for the environment, employees, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Social Services Association has continuously awarded the "15 Years + United in Care" emblem to The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) is committed to properly managing the environmental impact of its operations, and its internal "Green Office Guidelines" provide guidance to employees on resource utilization and waste generation of office waste. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) has integrated environmental factors into the design, operation, and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. When renovating the office, reuse existing furniture and finishing materials as much as possible to reduce waste generation, and prioritize the selection of environmentally friendly building and decorative materials. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) has consistently followed this practice, and in 2021 and 2022, the office for the portion of its second phase renovation at the international financial center was awarded LEED 7 and the "Green Building Council Interior Assessment" 8 certification. Through the adoption of new technologies and the effective utilization of existing technologies to improve energy efficiency, it remains one of the key focuses of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank). In addition to promoting good habits, such as turning off unnecessary lighting devices within the work area outside of working hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include using fluorescent lighting fixtures, motion sensors, setting the air conditioning room temperature to an appropriate level, and utilizing energy in the information technology network infrastructure. The energy consumption of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) continues to decrease, reaching 2.59 megawatt-hours per person in 2023, a 29.7% decrease from the 2015 criteria (Figure 1). Based on the nature of the daily operations of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank), its greenhouse gas emissions primarily originate from greenhouse gas emissions caused by the electricity consumed, which is generated by fossil fuels. In 2023, the total emission intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuels and electricity was 1.48 tCO e10 per person, a decrease of 45.2% compared to 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardized equipment, office software, and meeting facilities, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) also adopts digital tools and technology, automates and streamlines workflows, and builds a digital work environment to enhance online collaboration within the institutional. The paperless meeting has become the main meeting method of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank). To further reduce paper usage and improve efficiency, all internal administrative affairs primarily adopt electronic processes. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) encourages employees to integrate into green and digitalized work models, replacing paper documents and communication with digital methods. The implementation of the electronic record backup system is also in progress. The aforementioned green and digitalization measures have brought positive results. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's paper density in 2023 was 11.55 kilograms per person, a significant decrease of 64.8% compared to 2015 (Figure 3). Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, most international activities have returned to in-person formats, and simultaneously, the development of Hong Kong's position as an international financial center must be promoted; therefore, relevant The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) employees inevitably need to travel overseas for official duties. To reduce carbon emissions caused by air travel, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) encourages employees to take direct flights or combine different official travel itineraries where feasible when participating in overseas activities. At the institutional level, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO e in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) participates in the "Gold Standard" 12 certified carbon offset program to offset the remaining carbon emissions caused by air travel. This project involves waste-to-energy, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) will continue to make similar arrangements in 2024. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank)'s procurement process considers sustainability and environmental factors. As part of the comprehensive review of the institutional procurement policies and procedures, the current practice of procuring green products has been established as a formal system and complies with the environmental standards of the government's "Green Procurement Checklist," particularly in the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. Furthermore, the tender evaluation criteria have also incorporated ESG factors and innovative suggestions that can enhance productivity and efficiency. Furthermore, all suppliers must commit to complying with environmental regulations. In accordance with the "4R" principles, namely Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) adopts a three-pronged approach to minimize waste generation and manage the disposal of waste generation. Furthermore, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) conducted two waste generation audits in 2022 and 2023 to assist in formulating targeted waste management strategies. Details of the non-hazardous waste generation produced, including general waste destined for landfills and various recyclable waste, are contained in the "Summary of Performance" section on page 56. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) first directly participated in the gift unwinding program of the office building management company in the international financial center in 2023. Employees have collectively submitted approximately 3,000 used but still in good condition banknotes. These banknotes will be distributed to a conservation organization for public use during the Lunar New Year next year. Given that the operation of The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) and its backup data centers constitute the main portion of the institutional's overall energy consumption, two data centers have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by green building environmental assessments for existing data centers, achieving optimal energy consumption efficiency (Power Usage Effectiveness, abbreviated as PUE) 13. In 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's two data centers received "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings, respectively, for "green building environmental assessments" based on the assessment guidelines issued in 2021. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) is the first and only institutional to receive such a rating in Hong Kong. Improving the energy efficiency of the two data centers has always been a focus of the technical team. For this, the team adopted green design in the renovation project and employed good operational practices that are energy-efficient to reduce PUE and achieve relevant goals, including 24-hour monitoring of the data centers' environment facilities and continuous improvement of environmental factors such as airflow and temperature settings. As the technical team continuously improves the energy utilization of the data centers, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) commissioned an external consultant in December 2021 to review and comprehensively assess the green level of the data centers, and to formulate recommendations to further enhance performance in all aspects. The research was completed in 2022. Shortly after completing its research, The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (or Central Bank) began preparing for the certification qualification for "green data centers" under the "green building environmental assessments" certification program. The certification process is very comprehensive and rigorous. During the full year of 2023, the technical team implemented optimization measures based on the recommendations of the consultant report to improve energy performance and the healthy elements of the working environment within the data centers.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency independently verified the 2023 environmental data ("2023 data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The 2023 data includes the total energy consumption for 2023, greenhouse gas emissions for scope 1 and scope 2, business aviation travel greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, generated non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), their respective densities, and the changes compared to the 2015 levels. Furthermore, the 2023 data also includes the amount of kitchen waste generated during that year, its intensity, and the change compared to the level when the kitchen waste recycling scheme was launched by the HKMA in November 2022. The greenhouse gas emission data of the HKMA is compiled according to the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol) accounting system jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council of Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covers data from January 1, 2023, to December 31, 2023, and also includes relevant data used for comparison of annual performance during the period from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2015 (excluding kitchen waste). The scope of verification covers a total of five office and warehouse assets, of which four offices are located in 1) International Finance Centre Phase II, 2) Harmony Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase I, and 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, while the warehouse is in 5) Lokesing Industrial Centre, located in Kwai Chung. The purpose of this verification is to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and supporting evidence from five selected assets. This verification work is conducted in accordance with the "International Verification Engagement Guidelines 3000 (Revised Edition)" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board, specifically the provision for "Verification engagements other than the audit or review of historical financial data." The verification procedure is designed to make opinions and summaries to obtain a reasonable degree of assurance. The verification process is determined according to the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The validation process involved tracing the selected sample data back to its source to test the integrity and accuracy of the data, as well as reviewing the basic procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducting reliability testing. The validation process also includes verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, visiting representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 data, and selecting representative data and information for verification. The relevant original data and supporting evidence were also thoroughly reviewed during the validation process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of information. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The verification team of the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency did not participate in the preparation of the 2023 data. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reasonably assures and summarizes that the 2023 data is substantially accurate and reliable. The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is sufficient. Shen Xiaoyin Review Supervisor Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency April 2024

The threat posed by climate change is imminent, making accelerated global climate action imperative. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record and the first year since industrialization that global temperatures exceeded pre-industrial levels by a critical 1.5 degrees Celsius. Meanwhile, although global greenhouse gas emissions have eased slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached a new high, highlighting the inadequacy of current measures to mitigate climate change. In the process of addressing global warming, the manifestation of climate-related risks will intensify, and the impact on economic and financial markets is difficult to predict. Furthermore, with the current tense geopolitical situation, the global economic landscape is becoming increasingly fragmented, energy security issues are feared to escalate, and with an uncertain economic outlook, all pose greater challenges for nations in addressing climate change. The process of low-carbon economic transition requires substantial and continuous financial support. The transformation challenges are most severe globally, particularly in Asia. As pointed out by the World Economic Forum, Asia is not only an engine of global economic growth but also the region most susceptible to the impacts of climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a key role in whether the global goal of achieving net-zero emissions can be successfully reached. As a leading international financial center in Asia, Hong Kong needs to strengthen its leading role and fully utilize the power of finance to support and drive transformation within the region. Therefore, the Monetary Authority published the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" last year, outlining our vision and roadmap for gradually integrating sustainable development concepts into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on strengthening the financial industry's capacity to address risks related to climate change, and on the other hand, focuses on assisting the industry in grasping related new opportunities. Furthermore, we set an example and play a leading role. The Monetary Authority's sustainable development work includes four areas: supporting the banking sector to move towards net-zero emissions, investing in a sustainable future, promoting net-zero financing, and advancing more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a key role in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and Asia, but it also faces numerous risks during the transition process. In the "Action Plan," we have set ambitious goals, requiring all banks to commit to achieving net-zero emissions in their operations by 2030 or earlier, and achieving net-zero emissions in financing by 2050 or earlier. Furthermore, we require all banks to enhance the disclosure of risks and opportunities related to climate change. Furthermore, while continuously strengthening the climate risk management of banks, we also provide guidance for the transformation planning of banks, assisting them to enhance their capacity to respond to transformation and better manage related risks. We are also currently undertaking preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong's sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, striving to further enhance transparency in the industry's related activities. Furthermore, we are optimizing the Hong Kong sustainable finance classification directory launched in May of last year to include more sustainable activities (including transition activities). We expect to guide more capital towards sustainable and transformative projects by providing clear guidelines. Climate change brings significant entity and transformative risks, which may affect the long-term financial performance and value of foreign exchange fund investment projects. Furthermore, it also brings opportunities for growth and a positive impact to the foreign exchange fund. Our experience proves that investment returns and positive sustainable impacts can be mutually aligned, without conflict. In view of this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the "investment portfolio" of the foreign exchange fund by 2050 or earlier, and in the "Action Plan," we pledge to support Asia's transformative climate transform through the investment of the foreign exchange fund. Currently, the proportion of sustainable investment in the investment portfolio has exceeded ten percent. To further promote sustainable investment within the region, the Monetary Authority established a strategic partnership with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and international financial institutions in November of last year to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition in the Asia region through joint investment. Furthermore, we published the first "Monetary Authority ESG Expectations" document in September of last year, further promoting fund managers to proactively exercise ownership rights and adopt good sustainable investment practices. Capital circulation is particularly important for accelerating the transformative within the region. As an international financial hub, and as the preferred location for issuers in Asia (including provincial and municipal governments in Mainland China) to issue international sustainable bonds, Hong Kong plays a crucial role in guiding capital to accelerate transformative within the region. The Action Plan outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the area's preferred sustainable development financing platform, and the goals of promoting sustainable financial innovation. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" to drive green bond innovation (including the issuance of the first batch of multi-currency digital bonds globally in February last year), to expanding the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Support Scheme" to transformative financing instruments in May last year, to the launch of the "Digital Bond Support Scheme" in November last year, we have consistently strived to encourage local issuers to utilize Hong Kong's financial platforms to raise the capital required for carbon reduction and transformative efforts. To achieve a robust transformative, in addition to capital and innovation, a inclusive and participatory sustainable development system is also required for support. This includes reliable sustainable development data, high-transparency information disclosure, and industry talent with relevant knowledge and skills. Here, in the "Action Plan," we commit to supporting the promotion of high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosures, and to endeavor to fill the gaps in sustainable finance talent and knowledge within the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosure, particularly by providing user-friendly climate disclosure templates to promote sustainable disclosure for small and medium-sized enterprises. We also launched the professional-level module "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the banks professional qualifications framework last November to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local bank employees. Furthermore, through the first Hong Kong Green Week held in February of last year and other activities, we have allowed various sectors to participate in discussions on sustainable development, thereby promoting cooperation and innovation. Within the Monetary Authority, we are committed to ensuring operations align with the vision of sustainable development. In our Action Plan, we commit to achieving net-zero emissions for our operations by 2030 or sooner, which is 20 years ahead of our original commitment. Furthermore, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainable disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap issued by the government. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and incorporated low carbon emissions as a screening factor in the procurement process. Furthermore, we continue to improve work efficiency through digitalization, cultivate a culture of sustainable development within the organization, and encourage employees to actively participate in sustainable development work. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and dramatic changes in geopolitics have added variables to global climate action. However, climate change is an undeniable fact and is gradually intensifying. In addressing climate change, the current situation does not permit us to be in the slightest slack. We firmly believe that promoting an orderly and inclusive transformative process will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on the Hong Kong financial system and bring opportunities for us in the process. Entering 2025, we will continue to strive forward, endeavor to promote sustainable development work, and deepen relationships with partners who share similar philosophies. Despite facing severe challenges, we will continue to be committed to supporting Hong Kong, Asia, and other regions in building a sustainable future.

Climate change is a major challenge facing the current generation. As an international financial center and a sustainable finance hub in the Asia region, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development across Asia and globally. The People's Bank of China announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan") in October 2024, outlining the People's Bank of China's vision in this area, including our future direction, the timelines for achieving the targets of each initiative, and how we expect the industry to collaborate in promoting related work. The People's Bank of China plans to consolidate the financial industry in Hong Kong and the People's Bank of China's own capacity to address Climate change risks through the formulation of strategic policies, strengthening regulatory links, and improving internal operations, and to promote the transformation of the Asia region towards a more sustainable economy. Through active participation in international and regional discussions, the People's Bank of China is also committed to exerting influence in formulating green and sustainable finance policies and standards at regional and global levels. As a banking regulatory authority, the People's Bank of China focuses on enhancing the banking sector's climate change resilience and supporting banks in maintaining safety and stability during their transition to net-zero emissions. Our primary tasks for 2025 include: - Launching a new round of special reviews on the bank's climate risk management practices and conducting a third round of consultation meetings to examine the extent to which the bank has implemented the relevant regulatory requirements of the People's Bank of China and to further strengthen the bank's climate risk management capabilities. To improve the work of the supervisory authority-led stress testing framework by incorporating climate risk stress testing into the supervision framework of the People's Bank of China. Continue to promote the work of incorporating climate factors into the supervisory review procedures of the People's Bank of China. Preparatory work is underway for the development of relevant regulatory requirements by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision for the disclosure framework on climate-related financial risks (third pillar) and the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards in the local banking sector. Completed the compilation of the new module GS-2 of the "Regulatory Policy Manual" to provide guidance for the bank's transformation planning. and- share best practices regarding climate risk management and the application of green financial technology with the industry. In addition to its role as a regulator of the banking sector, The People's Bank of China also plays a promotional role, striving to promote the development of a green and sustainable financial ecosystem and supporting banks in providing financing for transformation. We have published the first phase of the "Hong Kong sustainable finance classification directory," providing the industry with tools to identify green and sustainable economic activities, and to promote related financial flows. The People's Bank of China has launched the second phase of its classified catalog work to expand the scope, including incorporating transition elements, increasing green economic activities, and incorporating climate change adaptation goals. Furthermore, building upon the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the green finance technology competition in 2023, we will host another green financial technology event in 2025 to promote banks' adoption of green financial technology solutions. Hong Kong possesses superior conditions, supporting sustainable financing needs within the area. To consolidate this role, we will continue to assist the government in promoting the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme," which has expanded its scope to include sustainable projects, such as social responsibility initiatives. This move will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a model for other potential issuers in the region. Furthermore, we will continue to provide funding through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme," encouraging more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platforms to raise sustainable funds. We will also strengthen promotional efforts to encourage more government, institutional, and corporate entities from Mainland China and other regions to raise green finance in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will also continue to catalyze and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing funding to digital green bond issuers through the "digital bond financing program." Although the market demand for high-quality sustainable disclosures by institutions and corporations is increasing, the capacity and preparedness for sustainability disclosures vary among different entities, and some entities may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the People's Bank of China will continue to cooperate with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance cross-institutional supervisory group to make sustainable disclosures easier to grasp and more inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with more comprehensive climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainable disclosures templates and supporting tools. Explore how to utilize technology to make existing resources more convenient and user-friendly. and cooperate with local major industry organizations to provide industry-required training. The sustainable finance market is volatile, requiring the expansion of the local talent pool and the filling of knowledge gaps from Hong Kong to in the region. The People's Bank of China's main work in 2025 includes developing professional-level training courses for the "green and sustainable finance" module under the "banking professional competency framework" in cooperation with the banking sector, as well as identifying areas where the industry has a need for further training through the forthcoming research on "Future Banking Sector Talent 2026 to 2030" for banks. Furthermore, we plan to collaborate with key stakeholders to strengthen the promotion of the government-funded "green and sustainable finance training pilot program" and review the scope of the program. At the regional level, The People's Bank of China will continue to cooperate with international financial institutions through the "green commercial bank alliance" to launch specialized programs in the Asia region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted skills enhancement and training support, promoting community engagement, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in formulating roadmaps to make green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, The People's Bank of China commits the foreign exchange fund's "portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier to support the overall economic transformation. We will continuously enhance the sustainability of foreign exchange fund investments through pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment methods, primarily focusing on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that promote positive climate outcomes. The People's Bank of China is committed to setting an example in the work of institutions for sustainable development. In response to the timeline for accelerating the achievement of net-zero commitments announced in the "Action Plan," The People's Bank of China will gradually incorporate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting in a pragmatic manner, continuing to promote the sustainable development of institutions. Specifically, we will conduct a dual materiality assessment in 2025 to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring we focus on material topics. Furthermore, we will conduct energy audits and evaluate technology-based solutions to assess the significant impact of climate risks on our offices and operations, in order to enhance our climate change resilience and risk preparedness. We support the roadmap for sustainable disclosures issued by the government in Hong Kong and are actively undertaking preparations to make disclosures in accordance with ISSB standards. In 2025, The People's Bank of China will continue to uphold its commitment, selecting data centers for the planned upgrade projects based on energy efficiency and energy-saving principles. We will also expand digital measures to promote sustainable development and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and to improve the overall digital experience for our employees, banks, and the public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating these impacts. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and the wider Asia region through its multiple roles as a central bank institution, a banking industry regulator, a market facilitator, a responsible investor, and a sustainability institution. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has a sound sustainable development governance framework that leads the formulation of relevant strategies and policies for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Supervise the implementation of relevant measures. and ensure that the operations and working methods of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority incorporate sustainable development factors. To strive for good corporate governance, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has established a sound sustainable development governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency for related work. The governance framework ensures that the strategic planning and decision-making processes of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority are effectively integrated with sustainability factors, and that effective mechanisms are in place to monitor and evaluate the progress and outcomes of sustainability work. The sustainable development governance framework of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority includes: - the Foreign Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and relevant specialized committees, responsible for supervising the work of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, including the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's work in sustainable development, and submitting recommendations. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Governor of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, is responsible for leading the overall Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) strategies and policies of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority at the management level. In terms of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office is responsible for coordinating and supervising ESG-related work within the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office. Furthermore, regarding other functional areas, the relevant groups and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainable development measures related to the development of the bank and the market up to the operations of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority itself. At the cross-sectoral level, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) jointly initiated the establishment of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Institutional Steering groups responsible for coordinating the work of various financial regulatory bodies, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion of the scope of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's sustainable development work over the past several years, we hereby established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainable development work across the different functional areas of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. To provide guidance for the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans related to ESG matters in the four functional areas of the banking industry, green and sustainable finance ecosystem development, foreign exchange fund investment, and internal operations. Supervising the implementation of ESG-related plans by the various functional departments of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Assess the performance and effectiveness of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in achieving its ESG goals. and - supervise external communication strategy. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Governor of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, with three deputy governors serving as permanent members. Additionally, we will invite the executive assistants responsible for matters related to green and sustainable development to attend the Steering Committee meeting to report on the main achievements and future plans of their work. The Steering Committee regularly convenes meetings, and support is provided by the relevant working groups under the purview of the bank division, institutional development and operations department, foreign affairs department, and the Foreign Exchange Fund Investment Office of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainable development measures, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the Securities and Futures Commission jointly established steering groups in May 2020. The Steering groups, as an inter-agency platform, provide strategic direction and coordinate cross-sectoral work on how the financial industry should address climate and environmental risks, in order to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details regarding the work of the Steering groups, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the green and sustainable finance ecosystem."

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has always been committed to strengthening the capacity of the Hong Kong financial system to address climate risks, while also contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily operations, and therefore must proactively manage climate risks. Meanwhile, Banks play a crucial role in the financial system, guiding capital towards green and sustainability projects. As a banking regulatory body, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is particularly focused on building the capacity for Banks to address and manage climate risks, and is accelerating the work for Banks to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. In October, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), presenting the Monetary Authority's vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainability finance centre and support sustainability development across Asia and globally. The Action Plan includes eight major objectives across four aspects. To assist the industry in achieving the goals of the relevant Banks' policies, we have consistently carried out the following tasks. All Banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions in their operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero financed emissions by 2050 or earlier. In December, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will share good practices for transition planning with the industry and launch industry consultation on the draft of Section GS-2 "Transition Planning" of the "Regulatory Policy Handbook." This new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing the capacity of Banks to respond to the net-zero transition and related risk management. Furthermore, we are reviewing the supervisory review procedures used to assess and monitor the capital adequacy of Banks and determine their second-pillar capital requirements, with the objective of incorporating factors proposed by the Basel Committee regarding the effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and encouraging Banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks (including Transition Planning) to address climate risks. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has always been committed to aligning local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB standards) and the Basel Committee's third pillar disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is analyzing the latest developments in sustainability disclosures and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants to conduct a technical feasibility study on the adoption of ISSB standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the "Action Plan."
