In May, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority published the Hong Kong sustainability finance classification directory to address industry concerns regarding greenwashing and to assist in guiding capital flows towards green and sustainable activities. The classification catalog covers 12 economic activities across four industries, aiming to align with common green classification catalogs and the classification catalogs of mainland China and the EU, while also incorporating relevant elements to address local conditions. We have launched the second phase of work to expand the scope of the classification catalog, and are consulting with a broad range of stakeholders to further promote the flow of green and sustainability funding. During the year, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will further strengthen supervision of climate risks management in Banks and is committed to supporting Banks in building the capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and respond to climate change. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has also completed all work to incorporate climate risks into the supervision procedures of Banks in the two-year plan formulated in 2022. To promote the ability of Banks to strengthen their management of climate risks, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority shares good practices observed in specialized review and consultation meetings with the banking industries, mainly including: - Establishing a robust governance framework, clearly defining the responsibilities of the board of directors and senior management - Ensuring effective oversight of key areas related to climate-related risks (1) Promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies (2) Take appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) establish a strong climate risks culture within the organization. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority held a roundtable meeting on August focused on the management of climate risks. At the round table meeting, bank representatives and Hong Kong Monetary Authority participants exchanged views on several issues related to climate risks, including the challenges banks face in the management of climate risks, climate risk stress testing, Transition Planning, and finance. This round table meeting provided an interactive platform for information sharing and assisted the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's work on climate risks regulation and other related matters. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has launched a specialized review of the framework and practices for the management of climate risks by Banks, and assessed their robustness and adequacy according to the regulatory expectations set out in Section GS-1 "management of climate risks" of the Regulatory Policy Handbook. The specialized review covers the entire risk management process, including risk identification, quantification, monitoring, reporting, control, and mitigation, as well as climate risks scenario analysis and stress testing. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority held the second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of Banks implementing Module GS-1 "management of climate risks" of the Regulatory Policy Handbook, and to understand the challenges they are facing. The consultation meetings also cover the latest regulations and market developments in climate-related areas, including Transition Planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and the issue of greenwashing. We provide feedback and guidance based on the specific circumstances of the Banks to support their management of climate risks. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority completed the second round of banking industries climate risk stress testing (CRST) in 2024, with participation from 21 retail banks and 25 international bank group branches in Hong Kong. The results show that, under various scenarios (including the simultaneous occurrence of climate risks and a macroeconomic downturn), the Hong Kong banking industries continue to demonstrate strong resilience in defending against severe climate-related shocks. Compared to the CRST pilot program, participating Banks have significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. The report detailing the CRST results and the good practices observed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority during the process was published in February 2025. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority understands the numerous data and methodological challenges that Banks face in the management of climate risks, and therefore has been committed to various initiatives to promote the application of technology to address these challenges. To address the issue of lacking physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risks assessment, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched a physical risk assessment platform in May, enabling Banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will respond to user feedback and incorporate more local data to enhance the platform. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority collaborates with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green financial technology solutions by Banks and the overall finance industries. During the year, we published practical application guides and two "Compliance Technology Use Case Presentations" (English version), explaining the technological solutions for assessing Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) and sustainability, as well as managing greenwashing risks. We also hosted the third "FiNETech," gathering over 150 finance organizations and technology companies to explore green finance technology cooperation. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is well aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system; therefore, broader climate factors and scenarios should be incorporated into finance risk analysis and research to strengthen current monitoring efforts. In the process of continuously monitoring finance stability risks, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will take into account climate change and include analyses of climate-related risks in all finance stability reports. Through active participation in the scenario design and analysis working group under the "Central Bank and Regulatory Organization Green Finance Network" (NGFS), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority assists in further enriching climate scenarios, helping the central bank and regulatory organizations understand the impact of climate change on the macroeconomy and finance. In November, NGFS published the fifth edition of the long-term climate macro-finance scenarios to provide reference for forward-looking climate risks assessment. As a member of the Transition Planning working group under the Finance Stability Board, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority participates in analyzing the interplay between the transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to review climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has issued the "Green Technology Practice Guidelines for Banks" (English version) to provide finance organizations with best practices for utilizing green technology to promote their net-zero transition. In terms of research work, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority conducts multiple applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change on the finance industry and the overall economy. The research topics include the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in resisting monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the finance industry in transitioning to a low-carbon economy. The aforementioned research findings not only enhance our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability but also provide valuable insights into the green and sustainability finance ecosystem, aiding in the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, these studies help strengthen the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The research findings are also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through various channels, including international forums and the "Hong Kong Monetary Authority Research Memoranda." The Hong Kong Currency and Finance Research Centre (Research Centre), responsible for research work under the School of Finance, has published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. This study provides evidence indicating that low-emission firms can gain significant benefits from carbon pricing, highlighting their role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. This research is published in the Research Centre's "Insights from Monetary Research" and is shared with local and international scholars and policy researchers. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Liquidity Funding Arrangement Framework" is a collateralized reserve funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has incorporated sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral under this framework. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and promoting sustainable finance as the mainstream. Through participation in this area, we help promote policy dialogue between international and regional levels on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draw insights from it to enhance the climate adaptation capacity of the Hong Kong financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as the leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As outlined in the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to building Hong Kong into the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers both within the region and globally, supporting technological innovation in the green finance sector, enhancing industry sustainability disclosure, and expanding the local green talent pool, and addressing the knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. To build Hong Kong into the region's and global first-choice sustainable financing platform to catalyze sustainable finance innovation, support high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosure to fill the talent and knowledge gaps in the region's sustainable finance, and to demonstrate the government's commitment to addressing climate change, promoting green finance, and striving to develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable development and livable city, the government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. To date, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has assisted the government in jointly issuing green bonds valued at approximately US$28 billion, sold to institutional and retail investors. The raised funds are allocated to over 110 government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and recycling, energy efficiency, and energy saving. We seize every issuance opportunity, continuously innovating and expanding the characteristics of green bonds, including currency, maturity, and distribution channels, to lay the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the impact of the scheme and further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a hub for green and sustainable finance, the scheme's scope was expanded to include sustainable projects, and it was renamed the "Government Sustainable Bond Scheme" (Sustainable Bond Scheme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Scheme, the government annually publishes the "green bonds report," detailing the allocation of funds raised from green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority assisted the government in July in issuing institutional green bonds worth approximately US$3 billion under the Sustainable Bond Scheme. This is a series of three-currency issues covering different maturity bonds in RMB, USD, and EUR. This tranche of bonds attracted participation from various investor categories, with a strong subscription response, recording subscription amounts equivalent to over 15 billion USD. The RMB green bonds with maturities of 20 and 30 years were the first issuance by the government, are the longest RMB bonds issued by the government to date, provide a new benchmark for the market, and further demonstrate the role of the Sustainable Bond Scheme. These bonds further enrich the selection of offshore RMB investment products in Hong Kong. Furthermore, global investors have reacted enthusiastically to the green bonds issued by the government, reflecting the investor's affirmation of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. To encourage more borrowers within the district to utilize Hong Kong's financing platforms to raise sustainable development funds, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to implement the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme," launched in May 2021, to provide grants to eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. This program is widely welcomed by the industry; as of the end of 2024, the program has provided financing for approximately 500 issuances of green and sustainable debt instruments in Hong Kong, totaling over USD 140 billion. The program was extended for three years to 2027 in May 2024, and the funding scope was expanded to include transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the scheme is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries within the district to gradually reduce carbon by utilizing Hong Kong's transition financing platform. Funding has been approved for green and sustainable debt instruments totaling over USD 140 billion, issued in Hong Kong for approximately 500 issuances (as of the end of 2024)—extended for three years to 2027, and the funding scope has been expanded to include transition financing instruments. Concurrently, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has actively promoted the sustainable financing platform in Hong Kong, achieving favorable results in this endeavor. The Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued its fourth offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong in August, with a total value of 7 billion RMB, including 2.7 billion RMB in RMB green bonds, 1 billion RMB in sustainable bonds, and 900 million RMB in social responsibility bonds. In September, the Guangdong Provincial People's Government issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, with a total value of 5 billion RMB, including 1.5 billion RMB in RMB green bonds. In October, the Hainan Provincial People's Government also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, with a total value of 3 billion RMB, including 1 billion RMB blue bonds and 1 billion RMB sustainable bonds. The aforementioned bond issuance activity repeatedly highlights Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable finance between Mainland China and various parts of the globe. By leveraging the aforementioned measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as the preferred platform for sustainable finance in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Markets Association, Hong Kong continued to be the largest hub for the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds in the Asia region in 2024, with the total amount of related bonds arranged in Hong Kong reaching USD 43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the total in the region. To catalyze innovation in sustainable finance, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority assisted the government in issuing two series of landmark tokenized green bonds in 2023 and 2024, namely the first batch of tokenized government green bonds globally, and the first batch of multi-currency digital bonds globally. The issuance shows the government's support for asset digitalization and innovative technology in the green and sustainable finance areas for market participants in the region. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also launched the "Digital Bond Support Scheme" in November to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting the innovative development of Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance markets. The working groups for sustainability disclosure under the Green and Sustainable Finance cross-institutional steering group have consistently strived to adopt the "International Sustainability Disclosure Standards" (ISSB standards) in Hong Kong. The government issued the "Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap" in December 2024, providing a clear path for large public accountability entities to fully adopt ISSB standards no later than 2028. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has always worked closely with local and international partners to support entities at different stages of preparation to achieve high-quality sustainability disclosure, making sustainability disclosure more accessible and inclusive. It is worth mentioning that we continue to encourage the steering group's application of the "Private Company Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire" (questionnaire) launched in cooperation with CDP in 2022. This questionnaire provides user-friendly disclosure templates, facilitating sustainability disclosure for companies, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The questionnaire was launched in February 2024 in electronic format, facilitating online submission for enterprises (see the QR code below). The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is optimizing the questionnaire to be more user-friendly based on feedback from the industry and the latest international developments, with specific measures including selecting core questions from the questionnaire and providing common use scenarios for the questionnaire. Furthermore, we also strive to improve the compatibility of the questionnaire and other supporting tools on the steering group website. For more information regarding the questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, in practice, in accordance with the latest global standards, should make high-quality sustainability disclosure in its "Sustainability Report" to demonstrate its commitment to sustainable development. The report contains extensive content on operational risks related to climate from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, as well as plans and progress in implementing initiatives to achieve climate goals. For details regarding the sustainability disclosure of our own operations, please refer to the chapter "Sustainable Development" of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Given the rapid changes in the sustainable finance market, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is strengthening skills training for the banking sector and promoting knowledge sharing with other regulatory bodies and international stakeholders to fill knowledge and talent gaps. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local bank employees in sustainable finance, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, in collaboration with the Hong Kong Banking Association, launched the foundational level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" in July 2023. This module aims to assist professionals in the banking sector and the industry in acquiring knowledge and developing relevant professional capabilities in Green and Sustainable Finance in a more effective manner, and covers four main work areas: (1) Green and Sustainable Finance products and services; (2) Sustainability/Climate Risk Management; (3) Sustainability disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainability strategy, compliance, and control. Furthermore, the professional-level "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit targeting mid-to-senior level bankers responsible for related work was also launched in November. To provide necessary training to bank employees, the bank has learned to act as the managing body for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit and launched the foundational level training course for this unit in May. Following the launch of the professional-level program in November, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will collaborate with the banking sector in 2025 to develop professional-level training courses. To address the further skills and training needs of the banking sector, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is currently collaborating with the banking sector on the "Future Banking Talent 2026-2030" study, with the objective of publishing the research findings in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the document "Future Banking Sector Talent 2021-2025" published in June 2020. The results of this research will provide important references for the industry, assisting it in formulating and adjusting talent training strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking sector. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, in cooperation with the steering group, continues to assist in promoting the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme," subsidizing training in sustainable finance for employees, graduates, and students. As of December 2024, the program has 85 international and local courses registered as eligible training courses, and over 5,700 refund applications have been approved. The government announced in the "2025-2026 Fiscal Budget Proposal" that the program will be extended until 2028. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through local and international cooperation. As a founding member of the "Coalition for Building Sustainable Investment Capacity" (CASI), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussion topics revolving around the global sustainable finance market, policy frameworks, and innovative tools. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority supports the establishment of a branch of the "Glasgow Net Zero Finance Alliance" (GFANZ) in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage the GFANZ network and its expertise to enhance skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a major global asset holder and manager, the Monetary Authority actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Leveraging its experience in how financial performance and positive impact can mutually reinforce each other, the Monetary Authority adheres to a responsible investment philosophy when managing foreign exchange funds, prioritizes sustainable assets, and requires its external investment managers to actively exercise ownership rights over the assets. The Monetary Authority invests prudently according to the principle of "preserve principal first, long-term appreciation," believing that thorough consideration of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors helps reduce related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of the investment. As a firm signatory of the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the Monetary Authority is committed to advancing its responsible investment work. We place special emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of foreign exchange funds and pursue more optimal long-term risk-adjusted returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment tools to direct capital towards sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). The Monetary Authority contributes to the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by leveraging its role as a principal investor. In September, the Monetary Authority issued the "Monetary Authority ESG Expectations" and made the document public to investment partners through the annual ESG workshop and the Monetary Authority website. Investors, regulatory bodies, and international organizations with similar philosophies jointly develop industry operational standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment by the financial industry and central banks. Through these cooperative efforts, we are committed to promoting a future where finance and sustainability go hand in hand. The Monetary Authority announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" in October, outlining how the "portfolio" of foreign exchange funds can achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, and mobilize partner support for a low-carbon economic transition, further solidifying its commitment to investing in a sustainable future. The Foreign Exchange Funds Advisory Committee, chaired by the Director of the Ministry of Finance, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented in the investment management of the foreign exchange funds by the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. The primary guiding principles establish the tone for the Monetary Authority to practice responsible investment while also considering the investment objectives of the foreign exchange funds. The Investment Committee under the purview of the Foreign Exchange Funds Advisory Committee is chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority and is responsible for supervising the ESG and climate-related risks associated with foreign exchange funds investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policy, and monitors the implementation status through the regular meeting reports of the sustainable investment subcommittee of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office is chaired by the Chief Strategist and is responsible for coordinating and supervising all ESG work of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. The motions and progress of work discussed by the ESG Committee at the quarterly meeting will be reported to the President of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office. Furthermore, the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee, regularly convened, chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority, the President of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office, and the Chief Strategist, provides guidance on the ESG policies and measures of different functions within the Monetary Authority, including the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office, to implement the Monetary Authority's overall ESG objectives. The sustainable investment subcommittee and the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office collaborate closely in integrating ESG factors, and assist senior personnel of the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office in managing the ESG risks and opportunities, especially climate-related ones, for various investment projects: - Public Market Investments - The situation after credit, regulatory, and supervisory committees composed of senior personnel from the Foreign Exchange Funds Investment Office have reviewed the ESG factors integrated into credit risk models based on the opinions of the sustainable investment subcommittee, and the ESG status of fixed-income asset portfolios is monitored through regular reports from the risk management and supervision departments. Furthermore, the sustainable investment subcommittee also participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring process of external investment managers for stock portfolios from an ESG perspective (see Section "Promoting Active Exercise of Ownership" in the "Risk Management" section on page 39 for details). Private Market Investment - The Investment Committee, chaired by the Governor of the Monetary Authority, will consider the ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment recommendation. The Monetary Authority understands the physical and transition risks and related opportunities brought by climate change, which will affect the long-term financial performance of foreign exchange funds investment projects. The United Nations Environment Programme's "2024 Emissions Gap Report" predicts that unless there is a rapid global mobilization to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the global average temperature will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Policy changes, technological development, and behavioral shifts due to rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. At the same time, the frequency and severity of extreme weather events are increasing, also bringing additional physical damage and financial loss risks to investment projects. In the face of these challenges, governments and industries worldwide are shifting towards sustainable solutions, creating investment opportunities with potentially long-term prospects in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies, and sustainable infrastructure. The Monetary Authority believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the investment objectives of the foreign exchange funds, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG factors. The Monetary Authority has set a target for the "portfolio" of foreign exchange funds to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, and will continue to advance this objective through an orderly, multi-pronged approach (see Figure 3). The Monetary Authority announced the "Action Plan" in 2024, which solidified commitments and efforts related to the foreign exchange funds and climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the low-carbon economic transition, the Monetary Authority tends to proactively engage in communication rather than excluding or withdrawing investment from investment projects. Investing in sustainable future foreign exchange funds' portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier—actively expanding the scope and types of sustainable investments, particularly those focused on climate transition in public and private markets—integrating ESG factors into each investment decision, with particular consideration for the prospects of climate change and transition—establishing clear ESG expectations that comply with international standards and best practices, and requiring all external investment managers, investing companies, and trading counterparties to adhere to them—committing to reducing the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of foreign exchange funds' stock portfolios by 67% from 2017 levels by 2030 or earlier through investment support for regional transition—continuing to engage with external investment managers to optimize investment opportunities to drive the transition—continuing to discover and prioritize high-quality investment opportunities that promote Asian transition and have a positive impact on the global level. First, maintaining a diversified and stable asset portfolio plays a key role in achieving the primary investment objective of the foreign exchange funds. Directly excluding certain categories or industries will narrow the investable universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risk. Through compatible approaches, the Monetary Authority is able to seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transformation, possessing excellent technology and good corporate governance to respond to changing global climate trends, including companies in high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires a core "brown" industries transformation. Only exclude relevant investment projects or divestment without helping solve carbon emission problems. Conversely, the Monetary Authority supports these industries in their transformation to sustainable and low-carbon operating methods by investing strategic capital and actively exercising ownership rights, thereby bringing about beneficial changes for themselves and for the global economy. The net-zero investment policy has evolved from a preference for green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with reliable transition prospects to drive comprehensive decarbonization of the overall economy. As a global asset holder, the Monetary Authority understands the long-term resilience of asset portfolios, which relies not only on the portfolio's own adjustments but also on broad economic transformation. Although there is no perfect single solution, the Monetary Authority improved its responsible investment strategy in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive the transition while supporting foreign exchange funds and global net-zero goals. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including integrating ESG factors into fundamental analysis and guiding the decarbonization tilt of asset portfolios, as well as thematic investing in various asset classes that align with the path toward net-zero emissions. In the public markets, this may involve a tilt in asset portfolios towards ESG-leading or climate solution-providing companies, and coordinating with guiding to promote corporate transformation. In the private market, there may place greater emphasis on promoting transformative investment projects. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the Monetary Authority continues to seek investment opportunities that can promote the climate transition and simultaneously enhance the long-term resilience of foreign exchange funds asset portfolios. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the foreign exchange funds' portfolio, with financial performance aligning with that of the relevant asset portfolios (Figure 5). Public Market Investments - The Monetary Authority has launched an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and has extended the application of a customized low-carbon stock index to the other two asset portfolios managed by external investment managers. The Monetary Authority continues to seek to provide green, social responsibility, and sustainability (GSS) bonds that offer competitive returns while providing funding for sustainable projects (see the related case study in the "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds" section). Private market investment - The Monetary Authority is committed to building resilient long-term growth portfolios and seizing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. The Monetary Authority is again leveraging its extensive network and professional knowledge to actively seek and review investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including establishing strategic partnership collaborations with multinational organizations (see the section "Collaborative Response to Climate Challenges from Asia to the Globe" for examples). Passive investment portfolios using ESG indices as investment benchmarks—customized decarbonization strategies for passive and active quantitative investment portfolios not using ESG indices—active investment portfolios with governance as a theme—active ESG investment portfolios with a theme of sustainability and climate transition—projects with sustainability characteristics, such as renewable energy infrastructure, and green-certified buildings and warehouses—funds with themes of energy transition and decarbonization for the global, Asian, and Global South—green, social responsibility, and sustainability bonds—green bond funds managed by international organizations—the "Joint Loan Portfolio Management Programme" (MCPP) managed by an international finance company, focusing on sustainable projects in emerging markets—the "MCPP One Planet" project, providing climate-related investments by the Monetary Authority in green bonds issued by a semi-official institution in emerging markets in line with the Paris Agreement. The funds raised by the green bonds are allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading the old equipment of several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrade projects cover the optimization of monitoring and control systems and pump performance to generate positive environmental benefits in wastewater management, waste reduction, and recycling processes. In addition to continuous wastewater and sludge treatment, these facilities will process the dewatered sludge through composting or reuse to produce fertilizers, charcoal, cement, and other building materials, achieving a sludge recovery rate of up to 100%. These facilities also utilize the gas generated during the sludge treatment process to provide energy for the boiler and generate electricity. The Monetary Authority invested in green bonds issued by a multilateral development bank. This bond provides funding for multiple projects, including the repair of a national canal system. As one of the largest irrigation systems in the country, the canal is designed to divert excess water from the river to arid regions. The main objective of this project is to repair the increasingly deteriorated lining of the canal to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water use efficiency, and reclaim water-inundated areas. Furthermore, the project also provides skills training to local stakeholders, promoting the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation technologies such as micro-irrigation and sustainable farming methods.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to being a responsible and sustainable institution. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's key focus in 2024 for fulfilling one of its commitments is the plan to advance the target date for achieving net-zero emissions for the institution's operations to 2030, twenty years earlier than the original target, consistent with the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan." In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority also commits to fostering employee training and mental and physical well-being, striving to promote financial inclusion, and enhancing public financial literacy. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee) is chaired by the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and is the principal decision-making body for various organizational sustainability measures. To demonstrate the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's commitment to climate change, the Steering Committee approved the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's new target to achieve net-zero emissions for its organizational operations by 2030 or earlier, as part of the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" ("Action Plan"), in October 2024. At the departmental level, the Assistant President (Organizational Development and Operations) provides guidance for sustainable development measures in organizational operations, employee physical and mental well-being, and social engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The administrative unit serves as the coordinator and central hub for the execution, communication, and reporting of sustainable development measures by the organizational. A special team of green office staff and volunteer service groups, composed of employees from different operating departments, is responsible for providing another layer of support. The former is a platform for brainstorming suggestions on how to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of employee participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's commitment to the environment, employees, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Social Services Association has continuously awarded the "15 Years + Shared Heart Care" emblem to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's sustainable development strategy continues to adopt a structure composed of three pillars: environment, employees, and social responsibility. Focusing on carbon reduction and digitalization in the daily operations of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 or earlier—adopting green procurement requirements according to government guidance—promoting more environmentally friendly operational solutions within the financial industry and the broader society—building a proactive team and talent pool to achieve the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's strategic goals—fostering a work environment that promotes collaboration and inclusion, emphasizing diversity and strengthening employee belonging—providing a high-quality working environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle—cultivating a culture of social concern—incorporating social considerations into procurement procedures and supply chain management—promoting financial inclusion, and enhancing public financial literacy through consumer education activities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority is concerned about climate change and sets an example. In October 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced plans to advance the target date for its organizational operations to achieve net-zero emissions to 2030, twenty years earlier than the original commitment, as part of an Action Plan. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has revised the roadmap for transitioning towards net-zero, focusing on responsibly managing the impact of daily operations on the environment, concentrating on reducing carbon emissions, energy saving, and paper reduction, as well as waste recycling and reuse, while fully utilizing the improvements in the local power company's generation fuel mix. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has established a digitalized work environment to improve efficiency while simultaneously reducing the carbon footprint. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority understands the importance of cultivating a sustainable development culture, and therefore, through the continuous organization of promotional programs and activities, encourages employees to actively adopt practices that contribute to sustainable development. Under the primary 2030 net-zero emissions goal, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has consistently explored the adoption of carbon embedded tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and to pursue low-carbon procurement as much as possible. In this regard, since 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has fully offset the carbon emissions from air travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offset programs. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will expand carbon embedding and carbon offset programs to cover all other major carbon emissions. In addition to the environmental commitments related to actual operations mentioned above, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to promote the market's low-carbon transition by introducing procedures for electronic document submission and processing, as well as promoting electronic payments and the recycling of coins into the market. The remainder of this chapter details the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's strategies in leading environmental protection, as well as promoting the physical and mental well-being of employees and caring for society. Under the overall organizational risk management framework of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the risk committee, chaired by the President of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, is responsible for supervising and reviewing the potential risks and threats that the Hong Kong Monetary Authority faces in its daily operations, including those caused by climate change. To more effectively assess the impact of climate change on operations, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has identified different climate-related risks and reviewed the actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring continued operation, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority Office has designed integrated measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires, and other emergencies. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority regularly updates contingency plans and comprehensive measures, which encompass not only the offices but also communication and computer facilities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility drills to ensure employees are always prepared for the execution of contingency measures. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has consistently monitored the transition risks it faces by tracking greenhouse gas emissions generated by its operations, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's latest climate goal is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across scope 1, scope 2, and scope 3 related to organizational operations by 2030 or earlier. These targets were formulated using the methodology of the "Science-Based Targets Initiative." The Hong Kong Monetary Authority adopts the Greenhouse Gas Accounting System to measure and report organizational emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from gasoline vehicles. Given the nature of operations, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's main greenhouse gas emissions are scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions caused by the consumption of fossil fuels to generate electricity. Due to the absence of data from individual suppliers, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority adopted a conservative approach to estimate the scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital products) and services. Other relevant scope 3 emissions include waste transported to landfills and employees' air travel and commuting. For the detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024, please refer to the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and criteria for verification are stated in the "Verification Statement" attached at the end of this report. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority implements and adheres to the same climate-related standards that it expects the supervised banks and the financial system to comply with. As a first step towards green mobility, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority began replacing its gasoline vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this work in 2025 to achieve comprehensive green mobility. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to integrate environmental factors into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in the renovation projects in 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority reused existing furniture and finishing materials or purchased new items at a discounted price through trade-ins, reducing waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority regularly reviews the energy consumption and energy-saving measures of its offices and data centers, and in the 2024 data center facility upgrade project, adopts a modular design uninterruptible power supply system to further optimize the energy usage efficiency (Power Usage Effectiveness, abbreviated as PUE) of the data centers to obtain "Green Building Environmental Assessment" certification. This design can flexibly expand capacity, improve operational efficiency during partial loads, and be equipped with advanced refrigeration technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has enhanced internal virtual collaboration through digital work and streamlined workflows to effectively reduce paper usage. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, in accordance with the software update cycle of manufacturers, can extend the lifespan of the use of fluid and desktop devices, thereby extending the safe usage period of the devices. To reduce waste generated by the office, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority adheres to the "4R" principles, which are refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle, and regularly conducts waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has trash cans in convenient locations in the office to recycle different materials. To improve recycling rates, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority established beverage box and plastic fruit net bag recycling bins in 2024. Furthermore, starting from November 2022, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will send the collected kitchen waste to a recycling center in Hong Kong. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority participated in the Environmental Protection Administration's "Activity Waste Reduction Commitment" in May 2024, committing to take measures to reduce waste generated by various activities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to prioritize the procurement of goods that meet the environmental standards of the government's "Green Procurement List," especially electronic goods and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority encourages employees to carefully plan their itineraries, for example, by combining multiple trips when attending overseas activities. At the organizational level, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has been purchasing sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing annual air travel carbon emissions by approximately 10%. Furthermore, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority participates in the "Gold Standard" carbon offset programs to offset its remaining air travel carbon emissions. This plan focuses on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority arranged multiple learning activities for employees, such as lectures and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance employees' understanding of environmental sustainability issues. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority held its first "Green Month" in May 2024, starting from April 22, 2024, with the theme "Green Thinking, Green Living, Green Work." This is a good opportunity to demonstrate the commitment and motivation of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to promote sustainable development in the internal operations practice environment. The content of the entire event includes a "Sustainability Development BINGO scorecard" to encourage employees to practice green living, a "Save the Earth" quiz game, and a "Moss Ball" indoor plant care workshop originating from Japan. Additionally, we share the waste audit results and have the community recycling center operator introduce best recycling practices. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month," the Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched a recycling campaign lasting approximately six months in October, highlighting the responsible disposal of waste and reminding employees that changes in individual small habits can significantly improve the overall organizational recycling performance. One highlight of the event was the launch of the "Green 'Adapt' Action" short film, featuring insights from several senior executives on recycling tips. This activity also launches a series of screen saver programs, posters highlighting the design, online articles, and electronic prompts to remind employees to practice waste reduction and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority conducted a survey of employees to understand their awareness of sustainable development and to collect their opinions on proposed green office measures. The investigation results will assist in formulating future sustainable development training activities and waste disposal strategies. As the central bank organizational of Hong Kong, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority views itself as an important member in facilitating transformation, and is therefore committed to leading and accelerating the low-carbon transition, promoting sustainable development practices in the financial industry and society as a whole. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has introduced multiple measures to enhance the efficiency of external procedures. Following the successful launch of the "Shared Data Submission Platform" in 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will expand the platform's service scope in 2024 to encompass non-bank organizational entities, such as value-added payment tool operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The purpose of expanding the scope of platform services is to further simplify the submission process for organizational filings, provide a smoother experience for all users, and simultaneously reinforce the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's commitment to sustainable development. Other new measures launched in 2024 include the SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's questionnaires through a simplified submission process, and the intelligent information and document management system, which provides a central platform for advanced search and bank-related document functions for users.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency independently verifies the environmental data of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The data includes the total energy consumption for 2024, greenhouse gas emissions for scope 1 and scope 2, paper usage, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), and greenhouse gas emissions from air travel, along with their respective densities. Furthermore, the data also includes the scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), and employee commuting, and their corresponding intensities. The greenhouse gas emissions data of the HKMA are compiled according to the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, developed jointly by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council of Sustainable Development. The scope of verification collectively covers six office and warehouse assets, of which five offices are located in 1) International Finance Centre Phase II, 2) Harmony Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase I, 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and 5) Global Trade Centre, while the warehouse is located in 6) Lokesing Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance of the accuracy and reliability of the data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and supporting evidence from six selected assets. This verification work is conducted in accordance with the "International Verification Engagement Guidelines 3000 (Revised Edition)" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board, specifically the provision for "Verification engagements other than the audit or review of historical financial data." The verification procedure is designed to make opinions and summaries to obtain a reasonable degree of assurance. The verification process is determined according to the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The validation process involved tracing the selected sample data back to its source to test the integrity and accuracy of the data, as well as reviewing the basic procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducting reliability testing. The validation process also includes validating the internal data collection and management mechanisms, visiting representatives responsible for data preparation, and selecting representative data and information for verification. The relevant original data and supporting evidence were also thoroughly reviewed during the validation process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of information. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The verification team of the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reasonably guarantees the data and summarizes: - the data is substantively accurate and reliable; The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is sufficient. Shen Xiaoyin Review Supervisor Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency March 2025
